cau_hoi: What is the capital city of France?
giai_thich: Paris is the largest city and the political and cultural center of France, located on both banks of the Seine River in northern France. Paris is known as the "City of Light" and is one of the most visited cities in the world. Marseille is the largest port city in France, while Lyon is the third largest city.

cau_hoi: What is the capital city of the United Kingdom?
giai_thich: London is located on the banks of the River Thames, is the capital of the United Kingdom, and also the capital of England. The city has about 9 million inhabitants and is one of the largest financial centers in the world. Edinburgh is the capital of Scotland, which is part of the United Kingdom, but not the capital of the entire country.

cau_hoi: What is the capital city of Spain?
giai_thich: Madrid is located almost in the center of the peninsula, on a plateau about 650 m above sea level, making it one of the highest capitals in Europe. Madrid was chosen as the capital in the 16th century partly because of its central location. Barcelona is the second largest city and the capital of the Catalonia region, famous for Gaudí's architecture.

cau_hoi: Which sea separates Europe from Africa?
giai_thich: The Mediterranean Sea means "sea in the middle of lands" because it is surrounded by three continents: Europe, Asia, and Africa. The sea only connects to the Atlantic Ocean through a narrow strait in the west. The Mediterranean coastal region has a characteristic climate with hot, dry summers and mild, rainy winters, making it very suitable for growing grapes and olives.

cau_hoi: Which European country is famous for its windmills and tulip fields?
giai_thich: In the Netherlands, windmills were once used to pump water out of low-lying areas, helping people reclaim land from the sea. The Netherlands is also the world's largest exporter of tulips, even though this flower originates from Central Asia and Turkey. The name "Netherlands" in English means "the low lands."

cau_hoi: Which country has a shape resembling a high-top boot on the map of Europe?
giai_thich: The Italian peninsula extends into the Mediterranean Sea with a shape very similar to a boot, with the "toe" pointing towards Sicily and the "heel" being the Puglia region. The capital of Italy is Rome, which was once the center of the Roman Empire. This unique shape helps many students easily remember Italy's location on the map.

cau_hoi: What is the famous river that flows through the center of Paris?
giai_thich: The Seine River is about 777 km long, originating from the Burgundy region and flowing out to the English Channel. The banks of the Seine in Paris, with dozens of bridges and landmarks like Notre-Dame Cathedral and the Louvre Museum, have been recognized by UNESCO as a World Heritage site. The Thames flows through London, while the Danube flows through Vienna and Budapest.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the highest mountain range in Western Europe, spanning France, Switzerland, Italy, Austria, Germany, and several other countries?
giai_thich: The Alps stretch about 1,200 km, curving in a crescent shape through 8 countries. This is a young mountain range formed when the African plate collided with the Eurasian plate. The Alps have many glaciers and are the source of major rivers like the Rhine and Rhône. This mountain region is world-famous for skiing and mountaineering.

cau_hoi: What is the capital city of Germany?
giai_thich: Berlin is the most populous city in Germany, with about 3.7 million people. After World War II, the city was divided by the Berlin Wall until 1989. Frankfurt is the financial center, home to the European Central Bank, while Hamburg is the largest port city in Germany.

cau_hoi: Athens is the capital of which country?
giai_thich: Athens is one of the oldest cities in the world, with a history of over 3,000 years. On the Acropolis hill in the city stands the Parthenon temple dedicated to the goddess Athena, who is believed to have given her name to the city. Today, about one-third of Greece's population lives in the Athens metropolitan area.

cau_hoi: Which country has the largest area in Europe (and also the largest in the world)?
giai_thich: Russia spans both Europe and Asia with an area of over 17 million km². The territory in Europe (west of the Ural Mountains) accounts for about a quarter of Russia's total area, but is home to about three-quarters of its population. The European part of Russia alone is larger than any other European country.

cau_hoi: Which ocean lies to the west of Europe?
giai_thich: The Atlantic Ocean separates Europe and Africa from the Americas. The western coasts of countries like Portugal, France, Ireland, England, and Norway face this ocean. Northern Europe borders the Arctic Ocean. The westerly winds from the Atlantic bring moisture inland, resulting in a mild, rainy climate in Western Europe year-round.

cau_hoi: What is the capital city of Russia?
giai_thich: Moscow is the most populous city in Europe when considering only cities entirely located on this continent, with about 13 million residents. The city center features the Kremlin and Red Square. Saint Petersburg was the capital of Russia for about two centuries (1712 – 1918) before the capital was moved back to Moscow.

cau_hoi: What is the capital city of Portugal?
giai_thich: Lisbon is located at the mouth of the Tagus River flowing into the Atlantic Ocean and is one of the oldest capitals in Western Europe. In 1755, the city was heavily damaged by a devastating earthquake and tsunami. Lisbon is famous for its yellow trams climbing steep hills and its patterned tiled streets. Porto is the second-largest city, known for its Port wine.

cau_hoi: Which strait separates the British Isles from France?
giai_thich: The French call it La Manche ("the sleeve"), while the English refer to it as the English Channel. This is one of the busiest shipping routes in the world. Since 1994, the Channel Tunnel, approximately 50 km long, connects the two countries by rail, with about 38 km lying beneath the sea, making it the longest underwater tunnel in the world.

cau_hoi: Which city in Italy is famous for its hundreds of canals instead of streets and gondola boats?
giai_thich: Venice is built on about 118 small islands in a lagoon, connected by more than 400 bridges. The houses are built on millions of wooden piles driven deep into the mud. Today, Venice often experiences flooding due to the phenomenon of "acqua alta" (high water), prompting Italy to construct the MOSE mobile barrier system at the lagoon's entrance.

cau_hoi: Norway's coastline is famous for its deep fjords and steep cliffs created by glaciers. What is this type of terrain called?
giai_thich: Fjords are formed when massive glaciers carve deep valleys during the ice age, and when the ice melts, seawater floods in. Fjords are often very deep and have cliffs rising hundreds of meters on either side. The term "fjord" originates from Norwegian. Fjords can also be found in Iceland, Chile, New Zealand, Canada, and Greenland.

cau_hoi: Which country in Western Europe is often referred to as the "Land of Fog"?
giai_thich: England has a temperate maritime climate, characterized by dampness, many cloudy days, and drizzling rain, hence it is called the "Land of Fog." London was once famous for its thick fogs, sometimes mixed with coal smoke, like the "Great Smog" of 1952. Today, the air in London has become much cleaner thanks to anti-pollution laws.

cau_hoi: What is the longest river in Europe?
giai_thich: The Volga River is about 3,530 km long, entirely flowing within Russian territory and emptying into the Caspian Sea. Russians affectionately call it "Mother Volga." The Volga River basin is home to about 40% of Russia's population. The Danube River is about 2,850 km long, making it the second-longest river in Europe.

cau_hoi: What is the highest peak in the Alps, located on the border between France and Italy?
giai_thich: Mont Blanc means "White Mountain" because its peak is covered in white snow year-round, standing at about 4,805 m (the height varies a few meters depending on the snow and ice on the summit). The Mont Blanc Tunnel is approximately 11.6 km long, running through the mountain and connecting France with Italy. The town of Chamonix at the foot of the mountain hosted the first Winter Olympics in 1924.

cau_hoi: What is the smallest country in the world, completely surrounded by the city of Rome?
giai_thich: Vatican City covers only about 0.44 km², smaller than many parks, and has around 800 residents. It is the residence of the Pope, the head of the Catholic Church, featuring St. Peter's Basilica and the Vatican Museums. Vatican is protected by the Swiss Guard, known for their famous yellow, blue, and red striped uniforms.

cau_hoi: Which island nation in the North Atlantic is known as the "Land of Ice and Fire"?
giai_thich: Iceland has massive glaciers alongside dozens of active volcanoes, earning it the nickname "land of ice and fire." Despite its name meaning "land of ice," thanks to warm ocean currents, winters in the capital Reykjavik are not very cold, usually around 0°C. Iceland has about 380,000 inhabitants, making it one of the least populated countries in Europe.

cau_hoi: What is the capital city of Austria?
giai_thich: Vienna (Wien) is located on the banks of the Danube River and is known as the "capital of music" of the world, where composers like Mozart, Beethoven, Haydn, and Schubert lived and created. Vienna has been ranked multiple times as the most livable city in the world. The city is also home to many international organizations such as OPEC and the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA).

cau_hoi: What is the name of the peninsula that includes the two countries of Spain and Portugal?
giai_thich: The Iberian Peninsula is located in the southwestern part of Europe, separated from the rest of Europe by a high mountain range to the north and only about 14 km away from Africa to the south. The name Iberia may derive from the Ebro River (Latin: Iberus). In addition to the two countries mentioned, the peninsula also includes the Principality of Andorra and the British territory of Gibraltar.

cau_hoi: Which sea does the Danube River, the second longest river in Europe, flow into?
giai_thich: The Danube River originates from the Black Forest in southern Germany, flowing eastward and emptying into the Black Sea in Romania and Ukraine. Before reaching the sea, the river creates a vast delta, home to hundreds of bird species, particularly pelicans. The Black Sea is connected to the Mediterranean Sea through straits in Turkey.

cau_hoi: Which two countries primarily make up the Scandinavian Peninsula in Northern Europe?
giai_thich: The Scandinavian Peninsula is the largest peninsula in Europe, stretching about 1,850 km, with Norway in the west and Sweden in the east; a small part in the north belongs to Finland. Culturally, "Scandinavian countries" typically include Norway, Sweden, and Denmark, while "Nordic countries" also include Finland and Iceland.

cau_hoi: Which capital city in Europe was formed from two cities located on either side of the Danube River, merging in 1873?
giai_thich: Budapest, the capital of Hungary, was formed from the unification of three cities: Buda and Óbuda on the west bank (hilly) and Pest on the east bank (plain). The two banks are connected by several bridges, the most famous being the Chain Bridge. Budapest is also known as the "city of thermal baths" with over 100 natural hot springs.

cau_hoi: Which mountain range forms the natural border between France and Spain?
giai_thich: The Pyrenees mountain range is about 430 km long, stretching from the Bay of Biscay on the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea. The highest peak is Aneto, at about 3,404 m, located in Spain. The mountain range is home to the Basque people in the west, an ethnic group with a very ancient language. Due to the difficult mountain terrain, Spain and Portugal developed quite separately from the rest of Europe.

cau_hoi: Which small island nation in the Mediterranean, located between Sicily and North Africa, has Valletta as its capital?
giai_thich: Malta is one of the smallest and most densely populated countries in the world, consisting of three inhabited islands: Malta, Gozo, and Comino. Its strategic location in the Mediterranean has made Malta a target for many empires. The Maltese language is the only Semitic language (related to Arabic) that is an official language of the European Union and is written in the Latin script.

cau_hoi: Which city is home to many important institutions of the European Union, such as the European Commission?
giai_thich: Brussels, the capital of Belgium, is often referred to as the "capital of Europe" because it hosts the European Commission, the Council of the European Union, and the headquarters of NATO. The European Parliament meets in both Brussels and Strasbourg (France). Geneva (Switzerland) hosts many other international organizations, but Switzerland is not a member of the EU.

cau_hoi: The Ural Mountains, often considered the boundary between Europe and Asia, are located in which country?
giai_thich: The Ural Mountains run north-south for about 2,500 km, from the Arctic Ocean to near the Kazakhstan border. This ancient mountain range has been eroded, making it relatively low, with the highest peak at about 1,895 m. The Urals are rich in minerals such as iron, copper, and gemstones. In the city of Yekaterinburg, there is a landmark marking the boundary between the two continents.

cau_hoi: What is the largest freshwater lake entirely located in Europe?
giai_thich: Lake Ladoga in northwestern Russia, near Saint Petersburg, covers about 17,700 km², larger than the combined area of many provinces in Vietnam. During World War II, when Leningrad was besieged, a "Road of Life" was opened over the ice of the lake to supply food to the city. Nearby Lake Onega is the second largest lake in Europe.

cau_hoi: What is the largest island in the Mediterranean Sea?
giai_thich: Sicily (part of Italy) covers about 25,700 km², located at the "toe" of the Italian peninsula, separated from the mainland by the narrow Strait of Messina, which is about 3 km wide. The island is home to Mount Etna, the most active volcano in Europe. Sardinia is the second largest island in the Mediterranean, followed by Cyprus, Corsica, and Crete.

cau_hoi: What is the capital city of Poland?
giai_thich: Warsaw is located on the Vistula River, the longest river in Poland. The city was about 85% destroyed during World War II, after which the old town was meticulously rebuilt based on paintings and old documents, and it is recognized by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site. Kraków was the capital of Poland for many centuries before the capital moved to Warsaw.

cau_hoi: What is the capital city of the Republic of Ireland?
giai_thich: Dublin is located on the east coast of the island of Ireland, at the mouth of the River Liffey. Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, a territory of the United Kingdom in the northeast of the island. Ireland is known as the "Emerald Isle" due to its lush green pastures year-round thanks to its humid climate and abundant rainfall. Dublin is also the European headquarters for many major technology companies.

cau_hoi: Which Nordic country is known as the "Land of a Thousand Lakes," with about 188,000 lakes?
giai_thich: Finland has about 188,000 lakes larger than 500 m² and about 75% of its area is covered by forests. The lakes were formed when glaciers from the Ice Age receded, leaving depressions. The largest lake is Saimaa, home to the very rare Saimaa ringed seal. Finland has been ranked as the happiest country in the world for several years.

cau_hoi: What is the highest peak in Europe, located in the Caucasus Mountains in Russia?
giai_thich: Elbrus stands at about 5,642 m, and is an extinct volcano with two peaks covered by permanent snow. Elbrus is part of the "Seven Summits" (the highest peak of each continent) that climbers aspire to conquer. However, due to the debated boundary between Europe and Asia in the Caucasus region, some consider Mont Blanc (about 4,805 m) to be the highest peak in Europe.

cau_hoi: The Rhine River, one of the busiest waterways in Europe, flows into which sea?
giai_thich: The Rhine River is about 1,230 km long, originating from the Alps in Switzerland, flowing through Lake Constance, forming part of the border between Germany and France, then flowing through Germany and the Netherlands to empty into the North Sea. The mouth of the Rhine is home to the port of Rotterdam, the largest port in Europe. The Rhine Valley, with its many ancient castles on the hills, is recognized by UNESCO.

cau_hoi: Which large city lies on both the European and Asian continents, separated by the Bosphorus Strait?
giai_thich: Istanbul (Turkey) has about 15 million inhabitants, most of whom live on the European side. The Bosphorus Strait is about 30 km long, connecting the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara, and has many bridges and underwater tunnels linking both shores. Although it is the largest city in Turkey, Istanbul is not the capital; the capital is Ankara, located on the Asian side.

cau_hoi: Which sea is surrounded by Sweden, Finland, Russia, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Germany, and Denmark?
giai_thich: The Baltic Sea is a semi-enclosed sea with very low salinity due to the influx of freshwater from rivers and only connects to the North Sea through narrow straits around Denmark. In winter, the northern part of the sea (the Gulf of Bothnia) often freezes over. Amber (fossilized tree resin) has been found along the Baltic coast for thousands of years.

cau_hoi: Which capital of Northern Europe was built on 14 islands, connected by about 50 bridges?
giai_thich: Stockholm, the capital of Sweden, is located where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic Sea, earning it the nickname "Venice of the North." The old town, Gamla Stan, is situated on a small island in the center. Every year, the Nobel Prize ceremony (except for the Nobel Peace Prize) is held in Stockholm on December 10.

cau_hoi: What is the second smallest country in the world, located on the Mediterranean coast and surrounded by France?
giai_thich: Monaco is only about 2 km² in size, making it the most densely populated country in the world. It is famous for Monte Carlo, the Formula 1 race that runs through narrow streets, and is home to many wealthy residents. Monaco has been ruled by the Grimaldi family since 1297, one of the oldest royal families in Europe.

cau_hoi: How many countries does the Danube River flow through or form borders for, making it the most in the world?
giai_thich: The Danube River flows through or forms borders for 10 countries: Germany, Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia, Romania, Bulgaria, Moldova, and Ukraine. Four capitals located along the river are Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, and Belgrade. The famous waltz "The Blue Danube" by Johann Strauss II is considered Austria's "second national anthem."

cau_hoi: Which of the following capitals is NOT located on the banks of the Danube River?
giai_thich: Prague (the capital of the Czech Republic) is located on the Vltava River, a tributary of the Elbe, so the water in Prague eventually flows into the North Sea rather than the Black Sea. Prague is famous for the Charles Bridge, Prague Castle, and is known as the "City of a Hundred Spires." Vienna, Budapest, Belgrade, and Bratislava are the four capitals located on the Danube River.

cau_hoi: Besides Vatican City, which country is completely surrounded by Italy?
giai_thich: San Marino is located on the slopes of Mount Titano in northern Italy, covering about 61 km². Traditionally, it was founded in 301, making it one of the oldest existing republics in the world. San Marino has two heads of state at the same time, called "Captains Regent," who are elected every six months.

cau_hoi: Which strait connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Atlantic Ocean, where Europe and Africa are only about 14 km apart?
giai_thich: The Gibraltar Strait separates Spain from Morocco. The ancient Greeks referred to the two cliffs on either side of the strait as the "Pillars of Hercules," considering them the edge of the known world. Due to strong evaporation in the Mediterranean, a continuous flow of Atlantic water enters through the surface layer of the strait, while saltier water flows out below.

cau_hoi: What is the official capital city (federal city) of Switzerland?
giai_thich: Many people mistakenly think that Switzerland's capital is Zürich (the largest city) or Geneva (home to many international organizations). In fact, Bern is the "federal city," where the government and parliament are located. Bern's old town, with its arcaded streets stretching about 6 km, is recognized by UNESCO. The symbol of the city is the bear.

cau_hoi: How many national languages does Switzerland have?
giai_thich: Switzerland has four national languages: German (about 60% of the population), French, Italian, and Romansh (only about 0.5% of the population, mainly in the canton of Graubünden). Therefore, Swiss banknotes are printed in all four languages. The abbreviation "CH" for Switzerland comes from the Latin name "Confoederatio Helvetica" to avoid choosing one language.

cau_hoi: What language is primarily spoken in the Flanders region of northern Belgium?
giai_thich: Belgium has three official languages. The northern Flanders region speaks Dutch (often referred to as Flemish), the southern Wallonia region speaks French, and a small community in the east bordering Germany speaks German. The capital, Brussels, officially uses both French and Dutch. The language differences make Belgian politics quite complex.

cau_hoi: Which major river does the capital Kyiv of Ukraine lie along?
giai_thich: The Dnipro River is about 2,200 km long, making it the fourth longest river in Europe, originating in Russia, flowing through Belarus and Ukraine before emptying into the Black Sea. The river divides Ukraine into the "left bank" and "right bank." Kyiv is one of the oldest cities in Eastern Europe, once the center of the medieval Kievan Rus state.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the mountain range that runs in a crescent shape through Slovakia, Poland, Ukraine, and Romania, surrounding the Transylvania region?
giai_thich: The Carpathian Mountains are approximately 1,500 km long, making them the second longest mountain range in Europe (after Scandinavia if considering the entire Scandinavian mountain system, or the longest in Central and Eastern Europe). Most of the range is located in Romania. The forests here are home to many of Europe's brown bears, wolves, and lynxes. The Transylvania region is associated with the legend of Count Dracula.

cau_hoi: The term "geyser" in many languages originates from the name of a hot spring in which country?
giai_thich: The Geysir hot spring in southwestern Iceland is the earliest described geyser by Europeans; its name comes from an old verb meaning "to gush." Today, Geysir rarely erupts, but the nearby Strokkur erupts water up to 15 – 20 m high every few minutes. Geysers form when groundwater is heated by hot rocks underground.

cau_hoi: How many large and small islands does Greece have?
giai_thich: Greece has about 6,000 islands and islets, but only about 200 are inhabited. The islands are grouped into several archipelagos such as the Cyclades, Dodecanese, and Ionian. Due to its many islands and peninsulas, Greece has a very long coastline relative to its area, and the Greeks have a tradition of seafaring since ancient times.

cau_hoi: What is the largest island of Greece?
giai_thich: Crete is approximately 8,300 km² in size, making it the fifth largest island in the Mediterranean, located south of the Aegean Sea. The island features high mountain ranges, the Samaria Gorge, which is about 16 km long and famous among hikers, and pink sand beaches. Crete has a warm climate, produces a lot of olive oil, and is one of the places with a diet considered to be healthy.

cau_hoi: Which small principality is located in the Pyrenees mountains, between France and Spain?
giai_thich: Andorra is approximately 468 km² in size, entirely located in high mountains, with its capital Andorra la Vella at an altitude of about 1,023 m, making it one of the highest capitals in Europe. Notably, Andorra has two "co-princes": the President of France and the Bishop of the Diocese of Urgell in Spain. The official language is Catalan.

cau_hoi: Lake Léman (Lake Geneva) is a large freshwater lake at the foot of the Alps, located between Switzerland and which country?
giai_thich: Lake Léman has a crescent shape, with about 60% of its area belonging to Switzerland and 40% to France. The Rhône River flows into the lake at the eastern end and out at Geneva. In Geneva, there is the Jet d'Eau fountain, which is about 140 m high, a symbol of the city. The cities of Lausanne (home to the International Olympic Committee) and Montreux are also located along the lake.

cau_hoi: What is the capital city of Scotland?
giai_thich: Edinburgh is famous for the Edinburgh Castle built on an ancient volcanic rock and the Edinburgh Fringe Festival, the largest arts festival in the world. Glasgow is the largest city in Scotland. Cardiff is the capital of Wales, while Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland. The United Kingdom consists of four countries: England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.

cau_hoi: The Jutland Peninsula, connecting to the European mainland in the south, is the main land area of which country?
giai_thich: The Jutland Peninsula occupies most of Denmark's area, with the southern part belonging to Germany. Additionally, Denmark has over 400 islands, with the capital Copenhagen located on the island of Zealand. Denmark is quite flat: the highest point is only about 171 m. Lego toys were invented in the town of Billund on the Jutland Peninsula.

cau_hoi: Which sea lies between the Italian Peninsula and the Balkan Peninsula?
giai_thich: The Adriatic Sea is a long and narrow branch of the Mediterranean. The eastern shore of the sea belongs to Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia, Montenegro, and Albania, with thousands of islands, especially in Croatia. The name of the sea may originate from the ancient city of Adria in Italy. The Aegean Sea lies between Greece and Turkey, while the Tyrrhenian Sea is located to the west of the Italian Peninsula.

cau_hoi: Which river flows through the capital city of London?
giai_thich: The Thames River is approximately 346 km long, making it the longest river entirely in England. In London, the river is crossed by many famous bridges such as the Tower Bridge. To combat flooding from tidal surges, London has built the Thames Barrier with gates that can be raised and lowered. The Severn River is the longest river in the United Kingdom.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the mountain range that runs along the length of the Italian peninsula, acting as the "spine" of Italy?
giai_thich: The Apennine Range is about 1,200 km long, stretching from the north down to the tip of the peninsula. Many volcanoes and earthquakes in Italy are related to the geological activity of this region. The Alps are located at Italy's northern border, while the Dinaric Range runs along the eastern coast of the Adriatic Sea, through Croatia, Bosnia, and Montenegro.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the peninsula in southeastern Europe, which includes countries like Greece, Albania, Bulgaria, and Serbia?
giai_thich: The name "Balkan" comes from a Turkish word meaning "mountain," as the peninsula has a very mountainous terrain. This region is home to a rich tapestry of ethnicities, languages, and religions. The peninsula is surrounded by the Adriatic Sea, the Ionian Sea, the Aegean Sea, and the Black Sea. The small continental part of Turkey around Istanbul also lies on this peninsula.

cau_hoi: Approximately what portion of the Netherlands' territory is below sea level?
giai_thich: About 26% of the Netherlands' area is below sea level, and around 60% is at risk of flooding without dikes. The Dutch have built a system of dikes, dams, and windmills to pump water to create "polders" (land reclaimed from the sea). The famous saying goes: "God created the world, but the Dutch created the Netherlands."

cau_hoi: Which ocean current brings warm water from the tropics, making Western and Northern Europe much warmer than other regions at the same latitude?
giai_thich: The Gulf Stream originates from the Gulf of Mexico, flows along the US coast, and then crosses the Atlantic Ocean, continuing as the North Atlantic Current to Europe. As a result, ports in northern Norway do not freeze in winter, while regions at the same latitude in Canada or Siberia do. London is further north than Beijing but is warmer in winter.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the most active volcano in Europe, located on the island of Sicily?
giai_thich: Mount Etna is about 3,300 m high (height varies with eruptions), making it the highest volcano in Europe outside the Caucasus region. Etna erupts almost continuously, but the lava usually flows slowly. The fertile volcanic soil around the base is excellent for growing grapes, oranges, and olives. Stromboli is a volcano on a small island north of Sicily, known as the "lighthouse of the Mediterranean."

cau_hoi: The Faroe Islands, located between Norway, Iceland, and Scotland, are an autonomous territory of which kingdom?
giai_thich: The Faroe Islands consist of 18 volcanic islands with steep cliffs and very few trees. The islands have about 55,000 inhabitants, with the number of sheep exceeding that of people. The name "Faroe" is believed to mean "sheep islands." The islands have self-governing powers and are not part of the European Union, although Denmark is an EU member.

cau_hoi: What is the capital city of Finland?
giai_thich: Helsinki is located on the shores of the Gulf of Finland, just about 80 km from Tallinn (the capital of Estonia) across the sea, with many ferries connecting the two cities daily. Helsinki is the northernmost capital of the European Union. The city is famous for its white cathedral in Senate Square and the sea fortress of Suomenlinna.

cau_hoi: What is the longest river in Italy, flowing through the fertile plains in the north?
giai_thich: The Po River is about 652 km long, originating from the Alps near the French border and flowing into the Adriatic Sea. The Po Valley is the most important agricultural and industrial region in Italy, where rice is grown for making risotto. The Tiber River flows through Rome, while the Arno River flows through Florence and Pisa.

cau_hoi: Which country does Cabo da Roca, the westernmost point of mainland Europe, belong to?
giai_thich: Cabo da Roca is a cliff about 140 m high overlooking the Atlantic Ocean, near Lisbon. The Portuguese poet Luís de Camões described this place as "where the land ends and the sea begins." If including islands, the westernmost point of Europe lies in the Azores (Portugal) or Iceland, depending on the definition.

cau_hoi: Which country has the largest area entirely located in Europe?
giai_thich: Ukraine covers about 603,500 km², larger than the mainland territory of France (about 551,000 km²). Russia is much larger but spans both Europe and Asia. Ukraine has very fertile black soil (chernozem), earning it the title "breadbasket of Europe," and it is a major exporter of wheat, corn, and sunflower oil.

cau_hoi: Which country in Europe has the largest population?
giai_thich: Russia has about 145 million people, with around three-quarters living in the European part of its territory, making it more populous than any other European country. Germany has about 84 million people, making it the most populous country in the European Union. Following are the United Kingdom, France, and Italy, each with about 59 to 69 million people.

cau_hoi: Which country lies between Switzerland and Austria, and is one of the two "double landlocked" countries in the world (surrounded by countries that are also landlocked)?
giai_thich: Liechtenstein covers about 160 km² and is located along the Rhine River. To reach the sea, one must pass through at least two other countries. The other "double landlocked" country is Uzbekistan in Central Asia. Liechtenstein is one of the richest countries in the world per capita and is a leading producer of dentures.

cau_hoi: What is the capital of Slovakia, located by the Danube River, bordering both Austria and Hungary?
giai_thich: Bratislava is the only capital in the world that borders two other countries. Bratislava and Vienna are the closest capitals in Europe (besides Vatican City and Rome), only about 55 km apart. For many centuries, the city (then called Pressburg) was the coronation site for Hungarian kings. Ljubljana is the capital of Slovenia, and Zagreb is the capital of Croatia.

cau_hoi: What is the northernmost capital of a sovereign country in the world?
giai_thich: Reykjavik, the capital of Iceland, is located at a latitude of about 64°08' North. About two-thirds of Iceland's population lives in the capital region. Summers here have almost no darkness, while in winter, there are only about 4 to 5 hours of daylight. Thanks to geothermal energy, most buildings in Reykjavik are heated with hot water from the ground.

cau_hoi: The three Baltic countries are Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. What is the capital of Lithuania?
giai_thich: Vilnius has one of the largest Baroque old towns in Eastern Europe, recognized by UNESCO. Riga is the capital of Latvia and the largest city in the Baltic region. Tallinn is the capital of Estonia, famous for its medieval old town. In 1989, about 2 million people joined hands to form a chain approximately 675 km long connecting these three capitals, known as the "Baltic Way."

cau_hoi: What is the largest lake in Central Europe, referred to by Hungarians as the "Hungarian Sea"?
giai_thich: Hungary is landlocked, so Lake Balaton, which is about 77 km long, is the most popular summer vacation spot for locals. The lake is very shallow, with an average depth of only about 3 meters, allowing the water to warm quickly in summer. In winter, the lake's surface can freeze thick enough for ice skating. The area around the lake is also famous for its vineyards producing wine.

cau_hoi: Lake Constance (Bodensee), through which the Rhine River flows, is bordered by which three countries?
B: Germany, Poland, and the Czech Republic
giai_thich: Lake Constance is the third largest lake in Central Europe. Interestingly, the three countries surrounding the lake have never signed an official agreement regarding the border on the lake, making it one of the few places in the world without clearly defined borders. The lake features Mainau Island, famous for its flower gardens and tropical plants.

cau_hoi: Which river flows through Lake Geneva, then through Lyon, and empties into the Mediterranean Sea in southern France?
giai_thich: The Rhône River originates from the Rhône Glacier in Switzerland, flows into Lake Geneva, and then through France. In Lyon, the Rhône merges with the Saône River. Before emptying into the sea, the Rhône creates the Camargue delta, a wetland famous for its flamingos, white horses, and wild black bulls. The Rhône has a strong current and is widely used for hydroelectric power.

cau_hoi: What is the longest river in France, famous for its hundreds of ancient castles along its banks?
giai_thich: The Loire River is about 1,000 km long, flowing entirely within France and emptying into the Atlantic Ocean. The Loire Valley, known as the "Garden of France," is home to many famous castles such as Chambord and Chenonceau, where French kings of the Renaissance once lived. The Loire is considered one of the last "wild" rivers in Europe due to its minimal damming.

cau_hoi: Which river flows through the German cities of Dresden and Hamburg before emptying into the North Sea?
giai_thich: The Elbe River is about 1,100 km long, originating from the Krkonoš Mountains in the Czech Republic. Hamburg, the third largest port in Europe, is located about 100 km from the mouth of the Elbe River, but large ships can still enter. The city of Dresden along the Elbe is known as the "Florence on the Elbe" due to its stunning Baroque architecture.

cau_hoi: Which river forms a large part of the border between Germany and Poland?
giai_thich: After World War II, the Oder-Neisse border was established between Germany and Poland, officially recognized by a reunified Germany in 1990. The Oder River originates in the Czech Republic and flows into the Baltic Sea near the city of Szczecin. The Vistula River is the longest river that flows entirely within Poland.

cau_hoi: What is the longest river on the Iberian Peninsula, flowing through Spain and emptying into the Atlantic Ocean at Lisbon?
giai_thich: The Tagus River is approximately 1,000 km long, originating in eastern Spain, winding around the ancient city of Toledo, and then flowing into Portugal. The mouth of the Tagus River in Lisbon is very wide, creating a wonderful natural harbor. The Vasco da Gama Bridge spans the river mouth and is about 12 km long, once the longest bridge in Europe.

cau_hoi: What is the only river in Spain that can accommodate large ships, flowing through the city of Seville?
giai_thich: The name Guadalquivir comes from the Arabic "al-wadi al-kabir" meaning "the great river," a remnant of the Moorish rule in southern Spain. Thanks to this river, Seville was once the exclusive trading port with the Americas in the 16th and 17th centuries, making it one of the wealthiest cities in Europe. The river flows into the Atlantic Ocean, with its estuary being the Doñana National Park.

cau_hoi: Which river do the cities of Florence and the Leaning Tower of Pisa in Italy sit beside?
giai_thich: The Arno River flows through the Tuscany region, emptying into the Ligurian Sea. In Florence, the river is crossed by the Ponte Vecchio bridge, an ancient bridge with jewelry shops built right on it. In 1966, the Arno River caused significant flooding in Florence, damaging thousands of artworks and rare books. The Tiber River flows through Rome.

cau_hoi: Which island is the Shannon River, the longest river, located on?
giai_thich: The Shannon River is approximately 360 km long, flowing through central Ireland from north to south, making it the longest river in both the British Isles and Ireland. The river passes through many lakes and empties into the Atlantic Ocean through a wide estuary near the city of Limerick. The Severn River is the longest river in Great Britain, measuring about 354 km.

cau_hoi: The city of Saint Petersburg in Russia was built on the delta of which short river flowing from Lake Ladoga into the Gulf of Finland?
giai_thich: The Neva River is only about 74 km long but has a very large water flow, ranking third in Europe, as it carries water from Lake Ladoga to the sea. Saint Petersburg is built on about 40 islands of the delta, with hundreds of bridges, many of which are raised at night for ships to pass. The city is famous for its "white nights" in June.

cau_hoi: Where does the Volga River, the longest river in Europe, flow into?
giai_thich: The Caspian Sea is the largest saltwater lake in the world, not connected to the ocean, so the Volga River does not flow into the sea. The Volga delta is the largest delta in Europe, home to sturgeon, a fish known for its famous caviar. A system of canals connects the Volga to other seas, allowing ships to travel from Moscow to five seas.

cau_hoi: In which country is the Black Forest, the source of the Danube River, located?
giai_thich: The Black Forest (Schwarzwald) is a mountainous region covered with dense coniferous forests in southwestern Germany, named so because the thick forests obscure the light. This area is famous for cuckoo clocks, Black Forest cake, and the fairy tales of the Brothers Grimm. The town of Donaueschingen claims to be the "source of the Danube River."

cau_hoi: The Iron Gates gorge, where the Danube River cuts through the mountains, forms the border between which two countries?
giai_thich: At the Iron Gates gorge, the Danube River flows through a narrow and deep canyon between the Carpathian and Balkan ranges. This section of the river was once very dangerous for ships due to many rocky rapids. In 1972, Yugoslavia and Romania built a large hydroelectric dam here, raising the water level and submerging an inhabited island called Ada Kaleh.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the famous pyramid-shaped mountain on the Swiss-Italian border, believed to be the model for the Toblerone chocolate packaging?
giai_thich: The Matterhorn stands approximately 4,478 m tall, with four nearly vertical faces pointing towards the four cardinal directions. In 1865, Edward Whymper's team was the first to conquer the peak, but four members died on the descent. The town of Zermatt at the foot of the mountain prohibits gasoline-powered vehicles to keep the air clean.

cau_hoi: What is the highest mountain in Greece, which according to mythology is the home of the gods?
giai_thich: Mount Olympus is approximately 2,918 m high, located in northern Greece near the Aegean Sea. In mythology, the god Zeus and 11 other gods reside on its summit, hence it is called "the gods of Olympus." In 1938, it became Greece's first national park. Mount Athos is home to many Orthodox monasteries, accessible only to men.

cau_hoi: What is the highest mountain in the United Kingdom, located in Scotland?
giai_thich: Ben Nevis is approximately 1,345 m high, located in the Scottish Highlands, and is the remnant of an ancient volcano that has collapsed. The summit is often shrouded in mist and the weather changes rapidly. Snowdon (Yr Wyddfa) is the highest peak in Wales, while Scafell Pike is the highest in England.

cau_hoi: What is the highest mountain in Spain, located on the island of Tenerife in the Canary Islands?
giai_thich: Mount Teide is a volcano approximately 3,715 m above sea level. If measured from the ocean floor, it rises about 7,500 m, making it one of the highest volcanic islands in the world. Mulhacén (about 3,479 m) in the Sierra Nevada is the highest peak on the mainland of Spain. The Canary Islands are geographically close to Africa.

cau_hoi: What is the highest mountain in Slovenia, depicted on the national flag and coat of arms?
giai_thich: Triglav means "three heads," standing at approximately 2,864 m, located in the Julian Alps. The three white peaks of Triglav appear on Slovenia's coat of arms and flag. Slovenians have a saying that one is not truly Slovenian until they have climbed Triglav at least once.

cau_hoi: What is the largest island in Europe?
giai_thich: Great Britain covers approximately 209,000 km², making it the ninth largest island in the world, consisting of three countries: England, Scotland, and Wales. Iceland is the second largest island in Europe, followed by Ireland. Great Britain separated from the European mainland about 8,000 years ago when melting ice caused sea levels to rise and submerged the land bridge known as Doggerland.

cau_hoi: Which country does the Svalbard archipelago in the Arctic, home to more polar bears than people and the Global Seed Vault, belong to?
giai_thich: Svalbard is located roughly between mainland Norway and the Arctic. The town of Longyearbyen is one of the northernmost inhabited places in the world. The Svalbard Global Seed Vault is dug deep into a mountain to preserve millions of crop seed samples from around the world in case of disaster. Here, residents must carry protective measures against polar bears when venturing outside town.

cau_hoi: What is the largest island of Sweden, located in the Baltic Sea?
giai_thich: Gotland is approximately 3,000 km² in size, featuring the town of Visby with its well-preserved medieval walls, a UNESCO World Heritage site. In medieval times, Visby was an important trading center of the Hanseatic League. Bornholm is a Danish island, while Zealand is the largest island in Denmark, home to the capital Copenhagen.

cau_hoi: Which city in the Netherlands houses the government, parliament, and the International Court of Justice of the United Nations, despite not being the capital?
giai_thich: According to the constitution, the capital of the Netherlands is Amsterdam, but the government, parliament, and the king's working residence are all located in The Hague. The city is referred to as "the legal capital of the world" because it hosts the International Court of Justice in the Peace Palace, as well as the International Criminal Court. This is a rare case where the capital and the seat of government are two different cities.

cau_hoi: What traditional occupation is famously associated with the Sami people, the indigenous people of the far north of Europe (Lapland)?
giai_thich: The Sami people live in the northern regions of Norway, Sweden, Finland, and the Kola Peninsula of Russia. They have their own language, which is related to Finnish, and a tradition of singing "joik." For thousands of years, many Sami families have moved with reindeer between winter and summer pastures. Today, only a small portion of the Sami still engage in reindeer herding.

cau_hoi: In 2010, ash from the eruption of a volcano in Iceland caused hundreds of thousands of flights in Europe to be canceled. What was the name of that volcano?
giai_thich: The Eyjafjallajökull volcano is located beneath a glacier, so when it erupts, the lava meets melting ice, resulting in very fine ash. The wind carried the ash cloud towards Europe, causing about 100,000 flights to be canceled over a week, affecting millions of passengers, as the ash could damage aircraft engines. The long, hard-to-pronounce name of the volcano means "glacier on the island mountain."

cau_hoi: What is the capital of Bulgaria, located at the foot of Vitosha Mountain?
giai_thich: Sofia is one of the oldest cities in Europe, with a history of about 7,000 years, once known as Serdica during Roman times. The name Sofia comes from the ancient church of St. Sofia in the city, meaning "wisdom." Sofia has many hot mineral springs. Bucharest is the capital of Romania, while Skopje is the capital of North Macedonia.

cau_hoi: Which capital in Europe is still divided by a buffer zone controlled by the United Nations?
giai_thich: Since 1974, Cyprus has been divided into two parts: the south controlled by the Republic of Cyprus and the north controlled by Turkish Cypriots. The capital Nicosia is divided by the "Green Line," a buffer zone monitored by UN peacekeeping forces. Berlin was once divided by the Berlin Wall but has been unified since 1990.

cau_hoi: Chișinău is the capital of which country in Eastern Europe, located between Romania and Ukraine?
giai_thich: Moldova is a small landlocked country that speaks Romanian. It is one of the countries with the most developed grape growing and winemaking industries, with underground wine cellars stretching dozens, even hundreds of kilometers, such as Mileștii Mici and Cricova. The Transnistria region in eastern Moldova has declared independence but is hardly recognized by any country.

cau_hoi: Minsk is the capital of which country?
giai_thich: Belarus is located between Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia, and is landlocked. Most of the country is flat, with many swamps, lakes, and forests, hence it is called "the land of blue lakes." Minsk was almost completely destroyed during World War II and was rebuilt with wide Soviet-style boulevards.

cau_hoi: Tirana is the capital of which country in the Balkan Peninsula?
giai_thich: Albania is located along the Adriatic and Ionian Seas. The Albanian language is a distinct branch of the Indo-European language family, with no close relatives to any other language. The Albanian flag features a black double-headed eagle on a red background. Albania has hundreds of thousands of concrete bunkers built during the Cold War, some of which have now been converted into cafes and museums.

cau_hoi: The city of Sarajevo, which hosted the Winter Olympics in 1984, is the capital of which country?
giai_thich: Sarajevo is located in a valley between the Dinaric Alps, where a mosque, a Catholic church, an Orthodox church, and a synagogue are situated close together, earning it the nickname "Jerusalem of Europe." The city was besieged for nearly four years (1992 – 1996) during the Bosnian War, one of the longest sieges of a capital in modern history.

cau_hoi: Which country is the only remaining "Grand Duchy" in the world?
giai_thich: Luxembourg is headed by a Grand Duke, covering about 2,600 km², located between Belgium, France, and Germany. Despite its small size, Luxembourg is one of the countries with the highest per capita income in the world, thanks to its banking and finance sector. In 2020, Luxembourg became the first country to make all public transport free. The people speak Luxembourgish, French, and German.

cau_hoi: Russia's Kaliningrad region is an "exclave" located between which two countries?
giai_thich: Kaliningrad does not share a common border with the rest of Russia, lying on the Baltic Sea, between Poland and Lithuania. Before 1945, it was the city of Königsberg in Germany, the birthplace of philosopher Immanuel Kant. This region has the largest amber reserves in the world, accounting for about 90% of global amber production.

cau_hoi: The large dam, approximately 32 km long, completed in 1932, transformed the Zuiderzee bay of the Netherlands into the freshwater IJsselmeer. What is the name of this dam?
giai_thich: Afsluitdijk means "closure dam," preventing seawater from the Wadden Sea from flooding the low-lying land. After the bay became a freshwater lake, the Dutch continued to build dikes and pump water to create new land (polder) on the old lake bed. The dam has a highway on it, and in the middle stands a statue of the engineer Cornelis Lely.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the cold, dry wind that blows down the Rhône Valley into southern France, often clearing the sky?
giai_thich: Mistral (meaning "master wind") blows from the north downwards, intensifying as it passes through the narrow valley of the Rhône, reaching speeds of over 90 km/h. The wind clears the clouds, resulting in many sunny days in Provence, attracting artists like Van Gogh and Cézanne. The locals plant tall cypress trees to shield their fields from the wind.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the hot wind that carries dust from the Sahara Desert across the Mediterranean to southern Europe?
giai_thich: Sirocco originates from North Africa, dry and hot, but as it passes through the Mediterranean, it picks up moisture, making it humid and sultry when it reaches Italy, Malta, and Greece. The wind sometimes carries red sand from the Sahara, causing 'blood rain' when the dust mixes with raindrops. In Venice, the Sirocco wind can push sea levels up, contributing to flooding in the city.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the dry and warm wind that blows down the leeward side of the Alps, capable of melting snow very quickly?
giai_thich: When moist air is pushed up the opposite mountain slope, it cools and leaves rain and snow. As it crosses the peak and descends on this side, the air is compressed and heats up rapidly, becoming dry and warm. The Föhn wind can raise temperatures by more than 10°C in just a few hours. In Vietnam, the southwest monsoon (Lao wind) in the Central region forms similarly.

cau_hoi: The city of Rovaniemi in Finland, located right on the Arctic Circle, is famous as the 'official hometown' of whom?
giai_thich: Rovaniemi is home to Santa Claus Village, where the Arctic Circle is marked on the ground, and the post office receives hundreds of thousands of letters from children around the world each year. Rovaniemi is the capital of the Lapland region. In winter, it is a great place to view the Northern Lights, while in summer, there is a phenomenon where the sun almost never sets.

cau_hoi: What is the phenomenon called when the sun does not set all night during the middle of summer in areas north of the Arctic Circle?
giai_thich: Due to the Earth's axis tilting about 23.5°, during the summer in the Northern Hemisphere, areas near the North Pole are always facing the sun, so the sun does not dip below the horizon. The closer to the pole, the longer the duration of 'midnight sun'. Conversely, in winter, there is a period of 'polar night' when the sun does not rise. Norway is often referred to as the 'land of the midnight sun'.

cau_hoi: Nordkapp (North Cape), often introduced to tourists as the northernmost point of Europe, belongs to which country?
giai_thich: Nordkapp is a cliff about 307 m high on the island of Magerøya, overlooking the Barents Sea. In fact, the nearby Knivskjellodden extends slightly further north, and since both are on islands, the northernmost point of the European continent is Kinnarodden. Nevertheless, Nordkapp remains a popular tourist destination where visitors can witness the midnight sun.

cau_hoi: What country does the southernmost point of the European continent, Cape Tarifa, belong to?
giai_thich: Cape Tarifa is located at the strait connecting the Mediterranean Sea with the Atlantic Ocean, from where the mountains of Morocco in Africa can be seen across the sea. The winds blow very strongly through the strait, so Tarifa is known as the 'kite surfing capital' of Europe. If including islands, the southernmost point of Europe is Gavdos Island of Greece, south of Crete.

cau_hoi: Where is the 'Giant's Causeway', consisting of about 40,000 hexagonal basalt columns, located?
giai_thich: The columns were formed about 50 – 60 million years ago when volcanic lava cooled and contracted, cracking into polygonal columns, most of which have 6 sides. According to legend, the giant Finn McCool built this path to cross the sea to Scotland to fight another giant. This is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

cau_hoi: What type of rock primarily composes the famous white cliffs of Dover, overlooking the strait between England and France?
giai_thich: Chalk is formed from the shells of billions of tiny plankton (coccolith) that accumulated on the seabed during the Cretaceous period, about 70 – 100 million years ago. The name 'Cretaceous' actually derives from this type of rock. The cliffs rise to about 110 m, and are the first sight that travelers from France see when arriving in England.

cau_hoi: In which country are the Dolomites mountain range with its pale limestone peaks that turn pink at sunset located?
giai_thich: The Dolomites are located in northeastern Italy and are part of the Alps. The mountain range is named after the French geologist Déodat de Dolomieu, who studied the type of rock found here, later called dolomite. The phenomenon of the mountain peaks changing to pink and red at dawn and dusk is known as 'Enrosadira'. The Dolomites are a UNESCO World Heritage site.

cau_hoi: In which country are the Orthodox monasteries built on top of giant sandstone pillars located in Meteora?
giai_thich: Meteora means 'suspended in the air'. Since the 14th century, monks have built monasteries on top of hundreds of meter-high pillars. In the past, people and goods were hoisted up using nets and ropes; today, there are steps carved into the rock. Of the approximately 24 monasteries that once existed, only 6 are still active. Meteora is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

cau_hoi: Plitvice National Park, famous for its 16 cascading turquoise lakes connected by waterfalls, is located in which country?
giai_thich: The lakes at Plitvice are separated by natural barriers made of tufa limestone, formed by the deposition of calcium carbonate from moss, algae, and bacteria over thousands of years. These barriers continue to grow. The water color changes from turquoise to emerald depending on the mineral content and light angle. Plitvice was one of the first natural heritage sites recognized by UNESCO (1979).

cau_hoi: Lake Bled, with a small island featuring a church in the middle and a castle on a cliff, is a famous tourist destination in which country?
giai_thich: Lake Bled is located in the Julian Alps and features Slovenia's only natural island. Visitors reach the island by traditional wooden boats called "pletna" rowed by hand. Traditionally, the groom must carry the bride up 99 steps to the church on the island. Bled Castle, perched on a high cliff, is considered one of the oldest castles in Slovenia.

cau_hoi: The famous lake in Scotland associated with the legend of a monster named "Nessie" is which lake?
giai_thich: Loch Ness is approximately 37 km long and very deep (about 230 m), containing more freshwater than all the lakes in England and Wales combined. The water is very murky due to high peat content. The story of the Loch Ness monster became famous in 1933, but no scientific evidence has proven the existence of this creature.

cau_hoi: Lake Vänern, the largest lake in the European Union, is located in which country?
giai_thich: Lake Vänern covers approximately 5,650 km², making it the third-largest lake in Europe after Russia's Ladoga and Onega lakes. The lake was formed after the Ice Age. Vänern is part of the Göta Canal, which connects Gothenburg on the west coast to the Baltic Sea on the east coast of Sweden. Sweden has about 100,000 lakes of various sizes.

cau_hoi: The largest lake in Italy, located at the foot of the Alps between Milan and Venice, is which lake?
giai_thich: Lake Garda covers approximately 370 km² and has a warm climate that allows lemons and olives to grow along its shores, despite being quite far north. Lake Como has an inverted Y shape and is famous for its luxurious villas. The large lakes in northern Italy were all formed by glaciers that carved deep valleys during the Ice Age.

cau_hoi: The longest and deepest fjord in Norway, known as the "King of the fjords," is which fjord?
giai_thich: Sognefjord is about 205 km long from the sea inland, with a maximum depth of approximately 1,300 m. The cliffs on either side rise over 1,000 m, resulting in very little sunlight reaching many areas. One of its branches, Nærøyfjord, is very narrow and has been recognized by UNESCO along with Geirangerfjord as a World Heritage Site.

cau_hoi: The Białowieża primeval forest, where European bison were saved from extinction, is located on the border between which two countries?
giai_thich: Białowieża is one of the last large primeval forests that once covered the European plain. The European bison (wisent) went extinct in the wild in 1919 but was bred from a few dozen individuals in zoos and reintroduced into this forest. Today, there are hundreds of bison here, the heaviest land animals in Europe.

cau_hoi: The highest sand dune in Europe, Dune du Pilat, which is about 100 m high, is located in which country?
giai_thich: Dune du Pilat is located near Arcachon Bay on the Atlantic coast in southwestern France. The dune is about 2.7 km long and is gradually moving inland a few meters each year due to wind, burying trees and sometimes even buildings. From the top of the dune, visitors can see the sea on one side and a pine forest on the other.

cau_hoi: The largest glacier in the Alps, approximately 20 km long, is which glacier?
giai_thich: The Aletsch Glacier originates from the Jungfrau region and contains about 11 billion tons of ice. Like most glaciers worldwide, Aletsch is shrinking rapidly due to climate change, retreating by several meters each year. Scientists predict that by the end of the 21st century, most glaciers in the Alps may disappear. Vatnajökull in Iceland is not part of the Alps.

cau_hoi: The rocky island of Mont-Saint-Michel with a monastery on top, only connected to the mainland at low tide, is located in which region of France?
giai_thich: Mont-Saint-Michel is located at the mouth of a bay with one of the largest tidal ranges in Europe, with differences of up to about 14 m. When the tide rises, the water comes in very quickly, surrounding the island. The monastery was built over many centuries, starting from the 8th century. In 2014, a new bridge was built to replace the old causeway, allowing the sea to surround the island again.

cau_hoi: Which sea is considered the shallowest in the world, with a maximum depth of only about 14 meters?
giai_thich: The Sea of Azov is located north of the Black Sea, connected to the Black Sea via the Kerch Strait. The water is very shallow and less salty because it receives freshwater from the Don and Kuban rivers, so it can freeze in winter. The Sea of Azov used to be rich in fish due to its warm and nutrient-rich waters. The North Sea has an average depth of about 90 meters, much deeper than the Azov.

cau_hoi: What is a unique characteristic of the deep water layers (below about 150 – 200 meters) in the Black Sea?
C: Almost no oxygen, contains a lot of hydrogen sulfide gas
giai_thich: The surface layer is less salty (due to many rivers flowing in) and lies above a saltier and denser deep water layer, with the two layers hardly mixing. Therefore, most of the volume of the Black Sea lacks oxygen and contains hydrogen sulfide gas, with almost no organisms except for bacteria. Thanks to the lack of oxygen, ancient shipwrecks on the Black Sea floor are very well preserved, some being about 2,400 years old.

cau_hoi: The Skagerrak Strait lies between the Jutland Peninsula of Denmark and which country?
giai_thich: The Skagerrak Strait connects the North Sea with the Kattegat Strait, then through narrow passages around the islands of Denmark into the Baltic Sea. At the Skagen point in northern Denmark, visitors can see the two seas, Skagerrak and Kattegat, meet, creating a distinct boundary of waves. This is an important maritime route for the countries around the Baltic Sea.

cau_hoi: Which bay in the Atlantic Ocean, between the western coast of France and northern Spain, is famous for its storms and rough waves?
giai_thich: The Bay of Biscay has a continental shelf that drops sharply from shallow to deep, combined with strong westerly winds from the Atlantic, creating very dangerous large waves for ships, especially in winter. The western coast of Spain is the Basque Country and the Cantabria region, famous for its surfing beaches. Here, you can also observe whales and dolphins.

cau_hoi: Which sea lies between the tip of the Italian peninsula and the western coast of Greece, home to the island of Corfu?
giai_thich: The Ionian Sea is part of the Mediterranean, with some very deep areas: the Calypso Deep here is about 5,200 meters deep, the deepest point in the Mediterranean. The Ionian Islands of Greece, such as Corfu, Kefalonia, and Zakynthos, are famous for their clear blue waters and white cliffs. Navagio Beach on Zakynthos features a very famous shipwreck.

cau_hoi: Why does the Barents Sea, north of Norway and Russia, have the port of Murmansk that does not freeze year-round?
B: Because the seawater has a lot of salt
C: Thanks to the last branch of the warm North Atlantic current
giai_thich: Although located north of the Arctic Circle, the southern part of the Barents Sea does not freeze due to the warm water flow from the Atlantic. Therefore, Murmansk is an important seaport for Russia, operational year-round. Murmansk is the largest city in the world located north of the Arctic Circle. The Barents Sea is named after the Dutch navigator Willem Barentsz.

cau_hoi: The Isle of Man in the Irish Sea is famous for which special breed of cat?
giai_thich: The Manx cat carries a natural gene mutation that causes many of them to be tailless or have very short tails. The Isle of Man is a self-governing territory under the British Crown, but not part of the United Kingdom, with its own parliament called Tynwald, believed to be one of the oldest continuously operating parliaments in the world. The island is also famous for the TT motorcycle race.

cau_hoi: The Channel Islands, including Jersey and Guernsey, are located close to the French coast, but which country are they a Crown dependency of?
giai_thich: Jersey and Guernsey are remnants of the Duchy of Normandy from the medieval period, with a duke who was also the king of England. When the English king lost Normandy in the 13th century, the islands remained loyal to the British crown. Each island has its own government, laws, and currency. The Jersey and Guernsey cattle are world-famous for their rich milk and originate from here.

cau_hoi: The Balearic Islands, including Mallorca, Menorca, and Ibiza in the Mediterranean, belong to which country?
giai_thich: The Balearic Islands are one of the most famous beach tourist destinations in Europe, attracting millions of visitors each year. Mallorca is the largest island, with its capital Palma featuring a large Gothic cathedral overlooking the sea. The locals speak Catalan (a local dialect) alongside Spanish. The name Balearic may originate from the ancient stone-throwing people known for their slings.

cau_hoi: Madeira, the birthplace of footballer Cristiano Ronaldo, belongs to which country?
giai_thich: Madeira is a volcanic archipelago in the Atlantic Ocean, closer to the African coast than to Europe, but is an autonomous region of Portugal. The capital Funchal has a famous airport with a runway partially built on high pillars extending into the sea. Madeira has a warm climate year-round, known as the 'island of eternal spring', and is famous for Madeira wine.

cau_hoi: The Lofoten Islands of Norway, located north of the Arctic Circle, are famous for which traditional occupation?
giai_thich: Every winter, cod from the Barents Sea swim to the waters of Lofoten to spawn, creating a large fishing season that has lasted for thousands of years. The fish are hung to dry on wooden racks outdoors in the cold wind for about 3 months, becoming 'stockfish' that can be preserved for many years and exported to Italy and Nigeria. Thanks to the warm ocean currents, Lofoten is much warmer than other places at the same latitude.

cau_hoi: The island of Santorini in Greece has a crescent shape because it is the remnant of which geological structure?
giai_thich: About 3,600 years ago, a massive volcanic eruption caused the central part of the island to collapse, allowing seawater to flood in and create a circular lagoon known as a caldera. The villages with white houses and blue domes are perched on the high cliffs along the caldera's edge. The volcano is still active, with the small island of Nea Kameni in the center.

cau_hoi: The Shetland and Orkney Islands in the north belong to which part of the United Kingdom?
giai_thich: Shetland is the northernmost region of the United Kingdom, closer to Norway than to London. The islands were once part of Norway and Denmark until the 15th century, so the culture still bears many Nordic influences, such as the Viking ship burning festival 'Up Helly Aa'. Shetland is famous for the Shetland pony breed. Orkney has many Neolithic sites, such as the ancient village of Skara Brae, which is about 5,000 years old.

cau_hoi: The Wadden Sea, the largest tidal flat in the world, stretches along the coast of which three countries?
giai_thich: Every day when the tide recedes, vast mudflats and sandbanks emerge, allowing people to walk across the seabed from the mainland to some islands (with a guide). This is a stopover for millions of migratory birds and a habitat for seals. The Wadden Sea is protected by a chain of Frisian islands and is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

cau_hoi: What is special about the island of Surtsey off the coast of Iceland?
A: It is the most populated island in Iceland
B: The island was created by humans
C: The island is entirely made of ice
D: It was formed by a volcanic eruption underwater since 1963
giai_thich: Surtsey emerged from the sea during a volcanic eruption that lasted from 1963 to 1967. From the beginning, the island has been strictly protected, with only a few scientists allowed to visit, to study how plants, insects, and birds gradually inhabit a completely new land. Due to coastal erosion, the island is gradually shrinking. Surtsey is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

cau_hoi: Lough Neagh, the largest freshwater lake in the British Isles, is located where?
giai_thich: Lough Neagh covers about 390 km² but is quite shallow, providing most of the drinking water for Belfast. The lake is famous for eel fishing, a species that migrates from the Sargasso Sea across the Atlantic Ocean to here. According to legend, the giant Finn McCool scooped up a handful of earth and threw it into the sea, creating the Isle of Man, and the remaining depression became the lake.

cau_hoi: Lake Ohrid, one of the oldest and deepest lakes in Europe, is located on the border of which two countries?
giai_thich: Lake Ohrid is believed to have existed for over a million years and is home to many endemic species not found anywhere else. The town of Ohrid by the lake once had many churches, leading to the saying that there are '365 churches, one for each day of the year'. The lake and its surroundings are a UNESCO World Heritage site for both natural and cultural reasons.

cau_hoi: Which port city in Belgium is the largest trading and diamond cutting center in the world?
giai_thich: The diamond district in Antwerp is only about one square kilometer but has been the trading hub for most of the world's rough diamonds for decades. Antwerp is also the second largest seaport in Europe, located on the Scheldt River. The city's name is linked to the legend of the hero Brabo, who cut off the hand of a giant and threw it into the river.

cau_hoi: The oldest city in France, founded by the Greeks around 600 BC under the name Massalia, is which city?
giai_thich: Marseille is the second largest city and the largest seaport in France, located on the Mediterranean coast. The French national anthem is called 'La Marseillaise' because it was sung by volunteer soldiers from Marseille as they marched to Paris in 1792. The city is famous for its fish soup bouillabaisse and the limestone cliffs of the Calanques.

cau_hoi: The capital of Italy, Rome, is known as the city built on how many hills?
giai_thich: The seven hills of Rome are located east of the Tiber River, including Palatine, Capitoline, Aventine, Caelian, Esquiline, Quirinal, and Viminal. According to legend, Romulus founded Rome on Palatine Hill in 753 BC. Because Rome is famous for its seven hills, many other cities around the world also proudly claim to be 'the city of seven hills'.

cau_hoi: Which city in Belgium, with its medieval canal system, is known as the "Venice of the North"?
giai_thich: Bruges was one of the wealthiest trading centers in Europe during the 13th to 15th centuries, but when the river mouth connecting to the sea silted up, the city declined and "slept" for hundreds of years. As a result, the medieval old town was preserved almost intact and is now a UNESCO World Heritage site. Bruges is famous for its handmade lace and chocolate.

cau_hoi: In which century was the famous crescent-shaped canal system of Amsterdam constructed, during the period known as the "Golden Age" of the Netherlands?
giai_thich: The Amsterdam canal ring was planned in the 17th century when the Netherlands was the world's leading trading power. Three main canals form a crescent shape around the center, with over 1,500 bridges. The narrow, tall houses along the canals have hooks on the roofs to hoist furniture through the windows, as the staircases are too narrow. The canal ring has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2010.

cau_hoi: Which city is the headquarters of the International Red Cross and the World Health Organization (WHO)?
giai_thich: Geneva is one of the largest diplomatic centers in the world, with the European headquarters of the United Nations located in the Palace of Nations and dozens of international organizations. The Red Cross movement was initiated by Henry Dunant, a businessman from Geneva, after witnessing the suffering of wounded soldiers in the Battle of Solferino in 1859. The red cross on a white background is an inverted version of the Swiss flag.

cau_hoi: Which city is the most populous in the European Union (considering the city's administrative boundaries)?
giai_thich: Berlin has about 3.7 million residents within the city limits, more than Madrid (about 3.3 million) and Rome (about 2.8 million). The city of Paris, according to administrative boundaries, has only about 2.1 million residents due to its very small area, although the entire metropolitan area of Paris has over 12 million people, the largest in the EU. This shows that the method of calculating city populations can change ranking results.

cau_hoi: After the historic flood of 1953, which massive flood protection project was built in the Zeeland region of the Netherlands, considered a modern engineering marvel?
giai_thich: The flood of 1953, caused by a storm combined with a high tide, resulted in the deaths of over 1,800 Dutch people. The Delta Works consists of a series of dams, dikes, and storm surge barriers, taking nearly 50 years to complete. Notably, the Oosterscheldekering storm surge barrier has gates that can close during storms but are normally open to allow tidal flow, protecting the ecosystem.

cau_hoi: Which country produces the most olive oil in the world?
giai_thich: Spain typically produces about 40-50% of the world's olive oil, depending on whether it is a good or bad harvest year, mostly from the Andalusia region in the south with hundreds of millions of olive trees. The olive tree thrives in the Mediterranean climate: hot, dry summers and mild winters. Italy and Greece are the next largest producers, and Greeks consume the most olive oil per capita.

cau_hoi: What is the area of Europe, and what rank does it hold among the continents?
B: About 10 million km², the second smallest among the continents
C: About 30 million km², the second largest
giai_thich: Europe covers about 10.2 million km², only larger than Oceania. Despite its small size, Europe has about 745 million people and around 44-50 countries (depending on the counting method). Geologically, Europe and Asia are on the same landmass known as the Eurasian continent; the division into two continents is mainly due to historical and cultural reasons.

cau_hoi: Which bridge-tunnel combination, inaugurated in 2000, connects Denmark's capital Copenhagen with which city in Sweden?
giai_thich: The structure is about 16 km long, consisting of a 4 km underwater tunnel, an artificial island, and an 8 km cable-stayed bridge, accommodating both cars and trains. The tunnel was constructed near Copenhagen to avoid obstructing flights at the nearby airport and the passage of ships. The bridge gained worldwide fame thanks to the television series "The Bridge" from both countries.

cau_hoi: Which language does Hungarian belong to, that is not part of the Indo-European language family like most European languages?
giai_thich: Hungarian, Finnish, and Estonian belong to the Uralic language family (Finno-Ugric group), originating from the area near the Ural Mountains. These three languages have very different grammar; for example, Hungarian has about 18 noun cases and does not distinguish between masculine and feminine. Despite being in the same language family, Hungarians and Finns cannot understand each other's languages.

cau_hoi: Which language in the border region between Spain and France is considered an "isolate language," having no relatives with any other existing languages?
giai_thich: Basque (Euskara) is believed to have been present in this region before Indo-European languages arrived in Europe, making it one of the oldest languages in Europe. Currently, there are about 750,000 speakers of Basque. Catalan and Galician are both Romance languages, closely related to Spanish and Portuguese.

cau_hoi: Which Eastern European country's official language belongs to the Romance language group (Latin origin), closely related to Italian and French?
giai_thich: Romanian is a descendant of Latin brought by the Romans when they conquered the region of Dacia in the 2nd century. Even the name of the country "Romania" means "land of the Romans." Despite being surrounded by Slavic and Hungarian-speaking peoples, Romanian retains many words similar to Italian. Moldovan is essentially Romanian.

cau_hoi: In Iceland, how is a person's last name typically created?
A: From the profession of the grandparents
C: From the name of the father (or mother) plus "son" (for son) or "dóttir" (for daughter)
D: From the family name passed down through generations
giai_thich: For example, Jón's son would have the last name Jónsson, while his daughter would be Jónsdóttir. Therefore, in a family, the father, mother, and children often have different last names. Icelanders usually address each other by their first names, even the president, and the phone directory is arranged by first names rather than last names. Modern Icelandic is still very close to Old Norse spoken by the Vikings.

cau_hoi: Which country's flag is considered the oldest continuously used national flag in the world, featuring a white cross on a red background?
giai_thich: The Danish flag is called "Dannebrog." According to legend, the flag fell from the sky during a battle in 1219, helping the Danes to victory. The cross is shifted towards the flagpole, known as the "Nordic cross," which was later imitated by Norway, Sweden, Finland, and Iceland in different colors. The Swiss flag features a white cross centered on a red square.

cau_hoi: Which island nation's flag features a map of the island itself?
giai_thich: The flag of Cyprus has a white background with a copper-colored map of the island (as the island's name may be related to copper, a metal mined here since ancient times), below which are two olive branches symbolizing peace between Greek Cypriots and Turkish Cypriots. Besides Cyprus, Kosovo's flag also features a map of the country. These are rare flags that include a map.

cau_hoi: Only two countries in the world have square flags. One is Switzerland, what is the other?
giai_thich: The Vatican flag has two colors, yellow and white, with the white part featuring two crossed keys (symbol of Saint Peter) and the papal tiara. The Swiss flag has a white cross on a red background. However, when displayed at some international events like the Olympics, the Swiss flag is sometimes made rectangular to match other countries.

cau_hoi: Which country has the most time zones in the world (about 12 time zones)?
giai_thich: Although mainland France uses only one time zone, France has many overseas territories spread across the oceans, such as French Polynesia, Guyana, Réunion, and New Caledonia, resulting in about 12 time zones (13 if including Antarctica). Russia has 11 time zones, the most for a contiguous territory. China, despite its size, uses only one time zone.

cau_hoi: Which country's largest sovereign wealth fund, established from oil and gas sales in the North Sea, belongs to?
giai_thich: Since discovering oil in the North Sea in 1969, Norway has invested most of its revenue into the Government Pension Fund (commonly referred to as the oil fund), investing in stocks of thousands of companies worldwide. The fund is valued at over $1.5 trillion, equivalent to more than $250,000 for each Norwegian citizen. The government is allowed to use only a small portion of the annual profits, saving for future generations.

cau_hoi: Approximately what percentage of homes in Iceland are heated using geothermal energy?
