giai_thich: Iceland is located in a region with strong volcanic activity, so there are many sources of hot water underground. Hot water is piped to homes, even running under sidewalks in Reykjavik to melt snow in winter. Almost all electricity in Iceland comes from hydroelectric and geothermal sources. The famous Blue Lagoon contains wastewater from a geothermal power plant.

cau_hoi: Which European country generates most of its electricity from nuclear power plants, with a ratio of about 65-70%?
giai_thich: After the oil crisis in 1973, France decided to build a series of nuclear power plants to reduce dependence on imported oil. Today, France has about 56 reactors and is a major electricity exporter in Europe. In contrast, Germany closed its last nuclear reactor in 2023. Norway generates almost all of its electricity from hydroelectric sources.

cau_hoi: Which country produces about half of the world's cork (cork oak bark)?
giai_thich: Cork is made from the bark of the cork oak, which grows abundantly in the Alentejo region of Portugal. The bark is stripped without cutting down the tree, and it regrows after about 9 years, making it a sustainable resource; each tree can live for about 200 years. Besides wine bottle corks, cork is also used for flooring, footwear, and even insulation materials for spacecraft.

cau_hoi: The Rose Valley in Bulgaria is famous for producing what product, which accounts for a large portion of the world's output?
giai_thich: The Rose Valley near the town of Kazanlak, located between the Balkan Mountains and the Sredna Gora range, has an ideal climate and soil for the Damask rose. The flowers must be hand-picked in the early morning. It takes about 3 to 4 tons of rose petals to distill 1 kg of oil, making rose oil more expensive than gold by weight. The oil is used to make high-end perfumes.

cau_hoi: What type of red chili powder is a symbol of Hungarian cuisine, used to cook gulyás soup?
giai_thich: Paprika is widely grown in the regions around Szeged and Kalocsa in southern Hungary. The chili plant originated from the Americas and was brought to Europe after Columbus's voyages. Hungarian scientist Albert Szent-Györgyi isolated vitamin C from paprika and won the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1937. Gulyás is a beef soup with vegetables and plenty of paprika.

cau_hoi: Which country is the largest exporter of sunflower oil in the world?
giai_thich: Ukraine's fertile black soil is very suitable for growing sunflowers. Before 2022, Ukraine accounted for about half of the global sunflower oil exports; Russia was the second-largest exporter. When the war broke out, exports were disrupted, causing cooking oil prices to rise in many places around the world. The sunflower is also the national flower of Ukraine.

cau_hoi: Which country occupies about 3% of the area in Europe (the Eastern Thrace region), with the rest in Asia?
giai_thich: The European part of Turkey is located west of the Bosphorus Strait, bordering Greece and Bulgaria, including most of Istanbul. Although it only accounts for about 3% of the area, this part has about 14% of the country's population. The main territory in Asia is the Anatolian peninsula. Turkey often competes in sports in European competitions.

cau_hoi: Besides Russia and Turkey, which of the following countries also has a small part of its territory in Europe (west of the Ural River)?
giai_thich: If we take the Ural River as the boundary, a small part of western Kazakhstan lies in Europe, with an area larger than many European countries. Therefore, Kazakhstan is a member of the European Football Association (UEFA). Countries in the Caucasus region, such as Georgia and Azerbaijan, are also often considered to lie between the two continents, depending on how the boundaries are drawn.

cau_hoi: Which country has the largest area among landlocked countries entirely located in Europe?
giai_thich: Belarus covers about 207,600 km², twice the size of Hungary and nearly three times that of Austria. The country has about 10,000 lakes and many swamps, especially in the southern Polesia region. Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world but only has a small part in Europe. Europe has about 16 to 17 landlocked countries, the most of any continent after Africa.

cau_hoi: The city of Bergen on the west coast of Norway is famous for being one of the what type of cities in Europe?
giai_thich: Bergen is situated between seven mountains and receives moist winds from the Atlantic Ocean, resulting in about 200 rainy days each year, with an average rainfall of about 2,250 mm. Locals joke that children in Bergen are born with an umbrella in hand, and there used to be an automatic umbrella vending machine here. Bergen is the gateway to the fjord region and has the Bryggen harbor area with its colorful wooden houses from the Hanseatic League.

cau_hoi: The climate type characterized by hot, dry summers and mild, rainy winters, typical in Italy, Greece, and southern Spain, is called what?
giai_thich: In summer, the subtropical high-pressure system shifts northward, bringing hot and dry weather. In winter, the high pressure retreats, and storms from the Atlantic bring rain. Typical crops include grapes, olives, and citrus fruits. The Mediterranean climate is also found in California, central Chile, South Africa (Cape Town region), and southwestern Australia.

cau_hoi: The Postojna Cave in Slovenia is home to which blind amphibian, locally known as "human fish" or "baby dragon"?
giai_thich: The olm is a completely aquatic salamander that lives in dark caves, with skin that is almost colorless, resembling pale human skin. Their eyes are covered by skin and are not visible. They can live for over 100 years and can go without food for about 10 years. In the past, when floods washed them out of their caves, locals thought they were the offspring of dragons living underground.

cau_hoi: The term "karst," used to describe limestone terrain with many caves like those in Ha Long Bay or Phong Nha, originates from the name of a plateau in which country?
giai_thich: The Kras plateau in southwestern Slovenia (extending into part of Italy) has many caves, underground rivers, and sinkholes formed when rainwater dissolves limestone. Scientists who first studied the area used the name of the region (in German, "Karst") to designate this type of terrain worldwide. Slovenia has over 10,000 explored caves.

cau_hoi: Where is the largest ice cave in the world, Eisriesenwelt (World of the Ice Giants), located?
giai_thich: Eisriesenwelt is located in the mountains near Salzburg, stretching about 42 km, but only the first kilometer contains ice. The ice forms due to cold winter winds blowing into the cave, freezing the meltwater that seeps in during spring. Inside the cave, the temperature is always below 0°C, even in summer. Visitors must bring lamps as the cave has no electric lighting.

cau_hoi: The Danube Delta, one of the largest and most intact wetlands in Europe, is mostly located in which country?
giai_thich: The Danube Delta covers an area of about 4,000 – 5,000 km², mostly in Romania, with a small part in Ukraine. It is home to the largest contiguous reedbed in the world and over 300 species of birds, including the largest pelican colonies in Europe. The delta continues to expand into the sea due to sediment deposits from the river. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

cau_hoi: The Blue Grotto (Grotta Azzurra), famous for its mystical blue light, is located on which island of Italy?
giai_thich: Sunlight enters the cave through a small opening under the water, with the seawater absorbing red light and leaving a blue hue, illuminating the entire cave in blue. The entrance to the cave is very low, and visitors must lie back in small rowboats to pass through. Capri is located in the Bay of Naples and has been famous since Roman times when Emperor Tiberius built a villa on the island.

cau_hoi: Neuschwanstein Castle, believed to be the inspiration for Disney's animated castles, is located in which state of Germany?
giai_thich: The castle was commissioned by King Ludwig II of Bavaria in 1869 on a rocky outcrop near the Alps, resembling a fairy tale castle. The king lived here for only a few months before mysteriously dying in 1886, while the castle was still under construction. Today, over a million visitors come to see it each year. Bavaria is the largest state in Germany, with Munich as its capital.

cau_hoi: A village in Wales is famous for having one of the longest place names in the world, consisting of 58 letters. What language is this place name in?
giai_thich: The full name of the village on Anglesey Island is "Llanfairpwllgwyngyllgogerychwyrndrobwllllantysiliogogogoch", which means "St. Mary's Church in the hollow of the white hazel near the whirlpool and St. Tysilio's Church by the red cave". The long name was created in the 19th century to attract tourists. Welsh is a Celtic language used on bilingual road signs throughout Wales.

cau_hoi: The Kiel Canal, the busiest artificial waterway in the world, connecting the North Sea to the Baltic Sea, is located in which country?
giai_thich: The Kiel Canal is approximately 98 km long, cutting across the Jutland Peninsula in the state of Schleswig-Holstein, allowing ships to avoid sailing around Denmark, saving an average of about 460 km. The canal was completed in 1895. In terms of ship traffic, the Kiel Canal is busier than both the Suez and Panama Canals combined, although most vessels are small to medium-sized.

cau_hoi: Which arid region in Almería, Spain, is often referred to as the "only desert in Europe" and has been the filming location for many Western movies?
giai_thich: Tabernas lies behind a mountain range that blocks moisture from the Mediterranean, receiving only about 200 – 250 mm of rainfall each year, with a landscape of bare hills and eroded canyons. The scenery resembles the American West, so during the 1960s and 1970s, hundreds of Italian "spaghetti western" films were shot here; many old film sets have now become amusement parks. Scientifically, this is classified as a semi-arid region.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the cold and strong wind that blows from the mountains down to the Adriatic coast, reaching speeds of over 150 km/h in the city of Trieste?
giai_thich: Bora forms when cold air from the eastern land spills over the Dinaric Alps and rushes down to the sea. In Trieste (Italy), when the Bora blows, people have to stretch ropes along some streets for pedestrians to hold onto, and many houses have their roofs secured with stones to prevent being blown off. The Bora creates white-capped waves in the Adriatic Sea even when the weather is sunny.

cau_hoi: Despite its small size, how does the Netherlands rank in the world for agricultural exports by value?
giai_thich: The Netherlands is smaller than the combined area of Nghệ An and Thanh Hóa provinces by several times, but thanks to modern greenhouse technology, drip irrigation, LED lighting, and automation, Dutch farmers achieve very high yields of fruits and vegetables. The Netherlands exports a lot of tomatoes, bell peppers, flowers, seed potatoes, and dairy products. Wageningen University in the Netherlands is one of the leading agricultural research centers in the world.

cau_hoi: Dettifoss waterfall, often considered the most powerful waterfall in Europe, is located in which country?
giai_thich: Dettifoss is about 44 m high and approximately 100 m wide, with an average flow rate of nearly 200 m³/second, and the water is gray due to the sediment from the Vatnajökull glacier. The roar of the waterfall can be heard from a great distance. The majestic scenery of Dettifoss appears in the opening scene of the science fiction film "Prometheus" (2012).

cau_hoi: The Rhine Falls, one of the largest waterfalls in Central Europe by flow rate, is located in which country?
giai_thich: The Rhine Falls is located near the city of Schaffhausen, with a height of about 23 meters and a width of approximately 150 meters. In summer, when the snow in the Alps melts, the water flow can reach about 600 m³/second. The falls were formed about 14,000 to 17,000 years ago, after the ice age, when the river was pushed into a new limestone bed. Visitors can take a boat to the rock in the middle of the falls.

cau_hoi: Which province of the Netherlands is the youngest in the country, created almost entirely from land reclaimed from the old IJsselmeer lake?
giai_thich: Flevoland was formed after the Dutch built dikes and drained part of the IJsselmeer lake in the 1950s and 1960s, officially becoming a province in 1986. The capital is Lelystad, while Almere is the largest new city, built since 1976. This area is one of the largest artificial land areas in the world, lying below sea level by several meters.

cau_hoi: Lake Peipus, one of the largest lakes in Europe, forms the border between Russia and which country?
giai_thich: Lake Peipus covers an area of about 3,500 km² (including two connected lakes), is quite shallow with an average depth of only about 7 meters, so it often freezes completely in winter. The lake is rich in fish, and the lakeside residents engage in ice fishing. On the Estonian shore, there are villages of 'Old Believers' from Russia, who fled here in the 17th and 18th centuries and are famous for onion farming.

cau_hoi: The Corinth Canal, which is only about 21 to 25 meters wide with steep cliffs on both sides, cuts through the isthmus connecting mainland Greece with which peninsula?
giai_thich: The Corinth Canal is about 6.4 km long and was completed in 1893, effectively turning the Peloponnese Peninsula into an island. The idea of digging the canal dates back to ancient times; Roman Emperor Nero initiated the project in 67 AD but abandoned it. Due to the canal's narrowness, large ships cannot pass through today, so it mainly serves tourism. The cliffs on both sides rise to about 80 meters.

cau_hoi: Which peninsula in northern Greece has a shape resembling a hand with 'three fingers' extending into the Aegean Sea?
giai_thich: The three 'fingers' of Chalkidiki are Kassandra, Sithonia, and Athos. Kassandra and Sithonia are famous for their white sandy beaches and pine forests. Athos is an autonomous monastic region that has existed for over 1,000 years and can only be accessed by boat. The philosopher Aristotle was born in the town of Stagira on the Chalkidiki Peninsula.

cau_hoi: The Campi Flegrei supervolcano ('Burning Fields'), where the ground continuously rises and falls, is located near which city in Italy?
giai_thich: Campi Flegrei is a massive caldera about 12 to 15 km wide, mostly located under residential areas and the bay west of Naples. Over 35,000 years ago, one of the largest eruptions in Europe occurred here. In the town of Pozzuoli, the ground has risen several meters over a few years, a phenomenon called 'bradyseism', causing the columns of an ancient Roman market to alternately sink and rise.

cau_hoi: What is the highest peak in Northern Europe (Norway, Sweden, Finland, Denmark, Iceland)?
giai_thich: Galdhøpiggen is about 2,469 meters high, located in the Jotunheimen National Park ('Home of the Giants') in southern Norway. The mountain is relatively easy to climb in summer, with many people reaching the summit in a day with guided tours over the glacier. Kebnekaise is the highest peak in Sweden, Hvannadalshnúkur is the highest peak in Iceland, and Halti is the highest point in Finland.

cau_hoi: What happened to Kebnekaise, the highest mountain in Sweden, that caused the map to change?
A: The mountain collapsed completely due to an earthquake
B: The southern peak, covered in ice, has been decreasing in height due to melting, making the northern peak the highest point
giai_thich: Kebnekaise has two peaks. The southern peak is covered by a layer of ice, which has long been higher than the northern rocky peak. Due to warming climate, the ice layer has been melting and thinning, and by around 2019, the southern peak became lower than the northern peak (about 2,097 meters). This is a clear example of how climate change can alter seemingly fixed geographical numbers.

cau_hoi: What is the highest peak in Germany, located on the border with Austria?
giai_thich: Zugspitze is about 2,962 meters high, located in the Alps in Bavaria. Visitors can reach the summit by cogwheel train or cable car, including a cable car with a record-high steel pillar. At the summit, there is a weather station, a small chapel, and a golden cross. Feldberg is the highest peak in the Black Forest, at only about 1,493 meters.

cau_hoi: What is the highest peak in Austria?
giai_thich: Grossglockner is about 3,798 meters high, with the Pasterze glacier, the longest glacier in Austria, at its foot. The high Grossglockner road, winding with dozens of hairpin turns, is one of the most beautiful mountain roads in Europe, open only in summer. This area is part of the Hohe Tauern National Park, the largest national park in the Alps.

cau_hoi: What mountain range is the highest peak in Poland, Rysy, located in?
C: Tatra Mountains (part of the Carpathian system)
giai_thich: Rysy has three peaks, with the highest peak at about 2,503 m located in Slovakia, while the peak in Poland is approximately 2,499 m and is the highest point in the country. The Tatra Mountains are the highest part of the Carpathian system, featuring small, clear glacial lakes. The town of Zakopane at the foot of the mountain is known as the "winter capital of Poland."

cau_hoi: Musala, the highest peak of the Balkan Peninsula (about 2,925 m), is located in which country?
giai_thich: Musala is located in the Rila Mountains in southwestern Bulgaria, slightly higher than Mount Olympus in Greece. The name of the mountain comes from Turkish, meaning "near God." Nearby is the famous Rila Monastery and the Seven Rila Lakes, a series of glacial lakes at varying altitudes. Bulgaria is a country with a mountainous terrain.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the vast plateau in south-central France, home to the UNESCO-recognized dormant volcano chain Chaîne des Puys?
giai_thich: Massif Central covers about 15% of France's area. The chain of about 80 volcanoes, Chaîne des Puys, with its rounded cone-shaped mountains and craters, is only a few tens of thousands of years old and has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2018. The Puy de Dôme peak is the symbol of the region. Massif Central is also the source of the Loire River.

cau_hoi: The Cliffs of Moher, approximately 214 m high overlooking the Atlantic Ocean, are one of the most famous attractions in which country?
giai_thich: The Cliffs of Moher stretch about 14 km along the west coast of Ireland, consisting of layers of shale and sandstone formed around 320 million years ago. The cliffs are home to thousands of seabirds, including the puffin. The cliff scenery has appeared in many famous films. Approximately one million tourists visit each year.

cau_hoi: The Åland Islands at the entrance to the Gulf of Bothnia are an autonomous, demilitarized region where Swedish is spoken, but belong to which country?
giai_thich: Åland consists of about 6,700 islands of various sizes, located between Sweden and Finland. In 1921, the League of Nations decided that Åland belonged to Finland but was granted extensive autonomy, keeping Swedish as the sole official language and being demilitarized. Åland has its own flag, postage stamps, and residents are exempt from military service. It is considered a model for peaceful dispute resolution.

cau_hoi: The Great St Bernard Pass in the Alps, connecting Switzerland with Italy, is famous for which breed of rescue dog raised by monks here?
giai_thich: For hundreds of years, monks at the hospice on the pass (at an altitude of about 2,469 m) have helped those crossing the mountains in snowstorms. They raised large dogs to guide and find people buried in the snow. The most famous dog, Barry, is said to have saved over 40 people in the early 19th century. Today, rescue operations use helicopters, but the St. Bernard breed is still raised here.

cau_hoi: The Wieliczka Salt Mine, which features a chapel with sculptures and chandeliers entirely carved from rock salt, is located in which country?
giai_thich: The Wieliczka Salt Mine near Kraków was continuously mined from the 13th century until 1996, with a tunnel system approximately 245 km long and reaching depths of 327 m. Miners carved the vast St. Kinga Chapel underground, complete with chandeliers made of salt crystals. Wieliczka was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1978.

cau_hoi: The largest island in Germany, famous for its white chalk cliffs painted by artist Caspar David Friedrich, is which island?
giai_thich: Rügen covers about 926 km² and is located in the Baltic Sea. The white chalk cliffs in Jasmund National Park, with the Königsstuhl peak rising about 118 m, were formed from marine sediment layers tens of millions of years ago. Friedrich's painting "The Chalk Cliffs on Rügen" (1818) is one of the most famous works of German Romantic painting. The island features ancient beech forests that are a UNESCO World Heritage site.

cau_hoi: The town of Hallstatt by the lake in Austria is famous for mining which mineral for about 7,000 years, considered one of the oldest mines in the world?
giai_thich: Salt was once very valuable for preserving food, making Hallstatt wealthy since prehistoric times. An early Iron Age culture in Europe (around the 8th – 6th centuries BC) is named "Hallstatt culture" after the ancient graves found here. Due to the narrow land between the mountains and the lake, the cemetery was so small that bones had to be placed in an "ossuary" with decorated skulls.

cau_hoi: The famous statue of David by Michelangelo was carved from white marble mined in which region of Italy?
giai_thich: The Apuan Alps around the town of Carrara in Tuscany have been mined for marble since ancient Roman times. The marble here is fine white with few impurities, highly favored by Renaissance sculptors; Michelangelo often personally selected each block of stone. Today, the white quarries on the mountainside look like snow from afar, and Carrara marble is still exported worldwide.

cau_hoi: According to the regulations of the European Union, sparkling wine can only be called "Champagne" if produced where?
giai_thich: Champagne is a "protected designation of origin," meaning the name is closely tied to the land and traditional production methods. Sparkling wine from other places must use different names, such as Cava (Spain) or Prosecco (Italy). The Champagne region has a cool climate and chalky soil, ideal for grape growing. The cellars carved deep into the chalk under the cities of Reims and Épernay are a UNESCO World Heritage site.

cau_hoi: The highest train station in Europe, at an altitude of about 3,454 m, known as the "Roof of Europe," is located where?
giai_thich: The Jungfrau railway was completed in 1912, featuring a tunnel about 7 km long carved through the Eiger and Mönch mountains. From the Jungfraujoch station, situated on a saddle between the Jungfrau and Mönch peaks, visitors can view the Aletsch Glacier stretching out. There is also an "Ice Palace" with ice sculptures and a scientific research station.

cau_hoi: The longest railway tunnel in the world, the Gotthard Base Tunnel (approximately 57 km), runs through the Alps in which country?
giai_thich: The Gotthard Base Tunnel was inaugurated in 2016 after about 17 years of construction, with sections lying as deep as approximately 2,300 m below the mountain peaks, where rock temperatures can reach around 45°C. The tunnel allows trains to travel faster from Zurich to Milan and shifts many goods from trucks to trains to protect the Alpine environment. Previously, the record was held by the Seikan Tunnel in Japan.

cau_hoi: The Millau Viaduct, the tallest bridge in the world (with a tower height of about 343 m, taller than the Eiffel Tower), is located in which country?
giai_thich: The Millau Viaduct spans the Tarn River valley in southern France, inaugurated in 2004, and is about 2.5 km long. The cable-stayed bridge was designed by engineer Michel Virlogeux and architect Norman Foster. On foggy days, the bridge appears to float above the clouds. The bridge helps alleviate severe traffic congestion every summer on the route from Paris to the Mediterranean.

cau_hoi: In 1989, the French National Geographic Institute calculated that the geographical center of Europe is located near the capital of which country?
giai_thich: According to this calculation, the center point is near the village of Purnuškės, about 26 km north of the capital Vilnius, which now has a monument and park. However, since the boundaries of Europe are defined in various ways, many other places such as Ukraine, Slovakia, Poland, and Belarus also claim to be the "center of Europe." This illustrates that the results depend on how we define the continental boundaries.

cau_hoi: Why is the coastline around the Bothnian Bay (between Sweden and Finland) gradually rising above sea level, causing Finland to "gain" a few square kilometers of land each year?
A: Due to global sea levels decreasing
B: Due to land reclamation by people
C: Due to volcanic eruptions under the sea
D: The Earth's crust is rising after the thick ice layer from the ice age has melted
giai_thich: During the ice age, a thick ice layer of about 3 km pressed down on the Earth's crust, causing it to sink. When the ice melted about 10,000 years ago, the Earth's crust slowly "bounced" back, rising about 8 – 9 mm each year in the Kvarken region. The Kvarken Archipelago and High Coast are UNESCO World Heritage sites as they are the best places to observe this phenomenon; old ports gradually become land.

cau_hoi: How long is Slovenia's coastline on the Adriatic Sea?
giai_thich: Slovenia's short coastline lies between Italy and Croatia, featuring beautiful small towns like Piran, Izola, and the port city of Koper. Despite its short length, Slovenia still has an important seaport serving many landlocked countries in Central Europe. In contrast, neighboring Croatia has a coastline longer than 1,700 km on land and over 1,000 islands.

cau_hoi: What is the narrowest point of the Strait of Dover, between England and France, approximately how wide?
giai_thich: On clear days, the white cliffs of England can be seen from the French coast. In 1875, Captain Matthew Webb was the first to swim across the strait without a buoy, taking nearly 22 hours as the current pushed him off course. Today, swimming across the strait is a famous challenge for long-distance swimmers, requiring escort boats.

cau_hoi: The largest glacier in Europe by volume, Vatnajökull, is located in which country?
giai_thich: Vatnajökull covers about 8% of Iceland's area, with some places being about 1,000 m thick. Beneath the ice are several active volcanoes, such as Grímsvötn and Bárðarbunga; when these volcanoes erupt, melting ice can cause sudden floods known as "jökulhlaup." South of the glacier is Jökulsárlón lake, where icebergs drift out to sea.

cau_hoi: The capital Riga of Latvia is located at the mouth of which river flowing into the Gulf of Riga?
giai_thich: The Daugava River is about 1,000 km long, originating from the hills in Russia and flowing through Belarus and Latvia. The Russians and Belarusians call it the Western Dvina River. Since the Middle Ages, it has been an important trade route connecting the Baltic Sea with the eastern lands, helping Riga become a wealthy trading city of the Hanseatic League, famous for its Art Nouveau architecture.

cau_hoi: The Douro River valley with its terraced vineyards, famous for producing Port wine, is primarily located in which country?
giai_thich: The Douro River originates in Spain and flows into the Atlantic Ocean at the city of Porto. The Alto Douro region is one of the oldest demarcated wine regions in the world (since 1756). The terraced vineyards have been built on steep slate hillsides over centuries and are now a UNESCO World Heritage site. In the past, wine barrels were transported down to Porto by flat-bottomed wooden boats called 'rabelo'.

cau_hoi: The Russian port of Arkhangelsk, the main seaport of Russia before the establishment of Saint Petersburg, is located near which sea?
giai_thich: Arkhangelsk is located at the mouth of the Northern Dvina River flowing into the White Sea. Since the 16th century, English and Dutch traders came here to trade, as it was the only Russian port open to the ocean at that time. The downside is that the sea freezes for about 5 to 6 months each year. The White Sea is named so perhaps because its surface is covered with white ice and snow during the long winter.

cau_hoi: What does the name of the city Innsbruck in Austria, which hosted the Winter Olympics twice, mean?
giai_thich: Innsbruck is located in the Inn River valley, surrounded by peaks over 2,000 m high in the Alps. The medieval bridge over the Inn River helped the city develop along the trade route from Germany to Italy. Innsbruck hosted the Winter Olympics in 1964 and 1976. The city's symbol is the 'Golden Roof' (Goldenes Dachl) covered with 2,657 gilded copper tiles.

cau_hoi: Where must the famous French blue cheese Roquefort be aged according to traditional regulations?
C: In the natural caves of Mount Combalou
D: On the summit of the Alps
giai_thich: Roquefort is made from sheep's milk and aged in limestone caves in the village of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon. The cracks in the mountain, known as 'fleurines', allow cool, humid air to circulate, creating conditions for the Penicillium roqueforti mold to develop into blue veins. In 1411, King Charles VI of France granted the villagers a privilege, one of the earliest regulations protecting the name.

cau_hoi: In Þingvellir National Park in Iceland, what can visitors dive in at Silfra fissure, between what two things?
D: Two tectonic plates of North America and Eurasia
giai_thich: Iceland is located on a ridge between the Atlantic Ocean, where the North American and Eurasian plates drift apart by about 2 cm each year. At Þingvellir, the rift is exposed on the surface, and the Silfra fissure contains water from glaciers filtered through volcanic rock for many years, so clear that you can see over 100 m. Þingvellir is also where Iceland's Althing parliament was established in 930.

cau_hoi: Which two cities in Spain are located on the North African coast, bordering Morocco?
giai_thich: Ceuta and Melilla are two autonomous cities of Spain, with the only land border between the European Union and Africa. Ceuta is located opposite Gibraltar across the strait, while Melilla is further east. Morocco claims sovereignty over these two cities. The population here is a mix of Spanish and North African cultures.

cau_hoi: The Azores archipelago in the Atlantic, belonging to Portugal, is located near the convergence of how many tectonic plates?
giai_thich: The Azores are located near the intersection of the North American plate, the Eurasian plate, and the African plate (Nubia), resulting in many volcanoes and earthquakes. The archipelago consists of 9 volcanic islands with crater lakes, hot springs, and lush pastures. The locals also cook stews by burying pots in the hot ground near hot springs for several hours. The Azores are famous for whale watching.

cau_hoi: The Azure Window, a famous natural limestone arch that appeared in the 'Game of Thrones' series, collapsed into the sea in 2017. In which country is it located?
giai_thich: The Azure Window was located on the island of Gozo in Malta, formed from a cave eroded by sea waves over thousands of years. The thin arch gradually eroded due to waves and rain, and by March 2017, it completely collapsed during a storm. This is an example of how coastal terrain is always changing: waves create caves, caves become arches, arches collapse into columns, and then columns also disappear.

cau_hoi: What is the special significance of the Rhine–Main–Danube Canal, completed in 1992?
A: It connects the North Sea to the Black Sea by waterway
B: It connects the Atlantic Ocean to the Pacific Ocean
C: It connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea
D: It connects the Baltic Sea to the Arctic Ocean
giai_thich: The canal is approximately 171 km long in Bavaria, Germany, connecting the Main River (a tributary of the Rhine) with the Danube River, crossing the European watershed through several locks. As a result, ships can travel from the port of Rotterdam on the North Sea to the mouth of the Danube River on the Black Sea, a journey of about 3,500 km. The idea of connecting the two rivers dates back to King Charlemagne in 793.

cau_hoi: What is a prominent feature of the tundra region in the far north of Russia?
D: A layer of permanently frozen ground, with only moss, lichen, and low shrubs
giai_thich: In the tundra, the summer is very short and cold, with only the surface layer thawing a few tens of centimeters, while below is 'permafrost'. Tree roots cannot penetrate deeply, so there are no large trees. This is home to reindeer, Arctic foxes, and migratory birds. When permafrost thaws due to warming climate, it releases methane, exacerbating climate change.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the vast plateau that occupies about 40% of Spain's area, where the capital Madrid is located?
giai_thich: The Central Meseta has an average elevation of about 600 – 800 m, surrounded by mountain ranges that block moisture from the sea, resulting in a harsh continental climate: hot, dry summers and cold winters. Spaniards have a saying about Madrid's climate: "Nine months of winter and three months of hell." The La Mancha region on the plateau is the backdrop for the novel "Don Quixote" with its windmills.

cau_hoi: Which two countries are connected by the Brenner Pass, the lowest pass crossing the main ridge of the Alps?
giai_thich: The Brenner Pass is about 1,370 m high and is located on an important transport route from Germany through Innsbruck to Verona in Italy, used since prehistoric times and the Roman era. Today, millions of trucks pass through the pass each year. A railway tunnel about 55 km long is being constructed underneath to relieve the road traffic, expected to be completed in the 2030s.

cau_hoi: What natural phenomenon is the Severn River estuary in England famous for, ranking as the second largest in the world?
D: Tidal range, with a difference of about 15 m
giai_thich: At the Severn River estuary, the water level during high and low tide can differ by about 15 m, second only to the Bay of Fundy in Canada. During strong tides, the sea water rushes into the narrow estuary, creating a wave known as the "Severn bore" that travels upstream, sometimes reaching several meters high, attracting surfers. Many projects have proposed building dams to harness tidal energy.

cau_hoi: The Kaali meteorite crater, formed when a meteorite fell thousands of years ago, is located on the island of Saaremaa in which country?
giai_thich: The Kaali crater has a diameter of about 110 m, filled with water, surrounded by 8 smaller craters created by fragments of the meteorite. The impact occurred when the area was already inhabited, leading researchers to believe the event may have entered ancient Baltic legends. Saaremaa is the largest island in Estonia, famous for its ancient windmills.

cau_hoi: What is special about the medieval town of Nördlingen in Germany in terms of geology?
C: Constructed inside an ancient meteorite crater about 15 million years old
giai_thich: The Nördlinger Ries crater has a diameter of about 24 km. The impact was so strong that it created a special type of rock called suevite, containing countless tiny diamond crystals; the town's St. George's Church is built from this stone. In 1970, astronauts preparing for the Apollo 14 mission came here to train in recognizing impact rocks.

cau_hoi: Where is the lowest point in Europe, about 28 m below sea level?
giai_thich: The Caspian Sea coast is about 28 m below ocean level because the Caspian Sea is a closed saline lake, with water levels depending on river inflow and evaporation. This area is part of the Caspian lowlands in southwestern Russia, characterized by a dry climate. The lowest point in the Netherlands is only about 7 m below sea level. The Dead Sea in the Middle East is the lowest point on land in the world.

cau_hoi: Which country has the town of Neum, the only territory that borders the sea, with a coastline of only about 20 km separating Croatia's coastline?
giai_thich: The strip of land Neum separates the Dubrovnik region from the rest of Croatia, causing travelers from Split to Dubrovnik to previously pass through two border checks. In 2022, Croatia inaugurated the Pelješac Bridge, about 2.4 km long, crossing the sea to connect the two territories without passing through Bosnia. Goods in Neum are cheaper, attracting many tourists to shop.

cau_hoi: What record does the Kola well in northwest Russia hold?
A: The deepest point ever drilled by humans into the Earth's crust (about 12.2 km)
B: The longest tunnel in the world
C: The first oil well in the world
D: The largest gold mine in the world
giai_thich: The drilling project began in 1970 to study the Earth's crust, reaching a depth of about 12,262 m in 1989. At that depth, temperatures reached about 180°C, hotter than expected, causing the rock to become plastic and the drill bit could not go deeper. Despite being very deep, the well only penetrated about a third of the continental crust thickness there. The well's mouth is only about 23 cm wide and has now been sealed.

cau_hoi: According to longitude, Spain should share the same time zone as the UK and Portugal, but it uses Central European Time (like Germany and France). When did this start?
giai_thich: In 1940, dictator Franco adjusted Spain's clocks to German time to show closeness to the German regime at that time, and this regulation has remained in place to this day. Therefore, the sun in Spain rises and sets later than the clock time, helping to explain why Spaniards often have lunch at 14 – 15 o'clock and dine very late, around 21 – 22 o'clock.

cau_hoi: Where was the highest officially recorded temperature in Europe, about 48.8°C in 2021, measured?
giai_thich: On August 11, 2021, a weather station near the city of Siracusa on the island of Sicily recorded 48.8°C, later recognized by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) as the temperature record for Europe. The previous record was 48°C in Athens in 1977. Scientists warn that extreme heatwaves in Europe are becoming increasingly frequent due to climate change.

cau_hoi: The tidal whirlpool Moskstraumen in the Lofoten Islands (Norway) inspired which English word meaning "giant whirlpool"?
giai_thich: Moskstraumen is formed by strong tidal currents flowing through a shallow strait between the islands, creating one of the strongest whirlpool systems in the world. The word "maelstrom" originates from Old Dutch/Norse, meaning "grinding stream." The writer Edgar Allan Poe wrote the story "A Descent into the Maelström" and Jules Verne also mentioned this whirlpool in "Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea."

cau_hoi: How many member countries does the European Union (EU) currently have?
giai_thich: The European Union has 27 members. The most recent member to join is Croatia (in 2013). Some wealthy European countries like Norway, Switzerland, and Iceland are not EU members but have close economic ties with the bloc. Many countries such as Ukraine, Moldova, Serbia, Albania, and Montenegro are in the process of applying for membership. Not all EU members use the euro.

cau_hoi: The Beerenberg volcano, the northernmost active volcano in the world, rises above the sea on which island?
giai_thich: Jan Mayen is a remote volcanic island in the Arctic Ocean, about 600 km from Iceland, with no permanent residents, only about 18 military personnel and meteorological station staff living on rotation. The Beerenberg volcano is approximately 2,277 m high, covered in glaciers, and last erupted in 1985. The island is named after the Dutch captain Jan Jacobszoon May.

cau_hoi: Including the islands, the northernmost point of Europe is Cape Fligely, which belongs to which archipelago?
giai_thich: Cape Fligely is located on Rudolf Island at a latitude of about 81°50' North, only about 900 km from the North Pole. The Franz Josef Land archipelago consists of about 190 islands, mostly covered in ice, discovered by an Austro-Hungarian expedition in 1873 and named after the Austrian emperor. The archipelago belongs to Russia and is protected as a nature reserve in the Arctic.

cau_hoi: According to the Svalbard Treaty (1920), what special rights do citizens of the signatory countries have on this archipelago?
A: To live, work, and do business there like Norwegian citizens, without a visa
B: To freely hunt all species of animals
D: To be exempt from all laws
giai_thich: The Svalbard Treaty recognizes Norway's sovereignty but grants citizens of the signatory countries equal rights in resource exploitation and economic activities. Therefore, Russia still maintains the coal mining town of Barentsburg on the archipelago. The treaty also prohibits the establishment of military bases here. Vietnam is not one of the original signatory countries, but the treaty remains open for participation.

cau_hoi: About 6 million years ago, the Mediterranean experienced a special event known as the "Messinian Salinity Crisis". What was it?
A: Cut off from the Atlantic Ocean and nearly dried up, leaving a thick layer of salt
D: Transformed into a giant freshwater lake
giai_thich: When the connection to the Atlantic Ocean was closed due to tectonic plate movements, the Mediterranean Sea evaporated significantly, with water levels dropping by kilometers, leaving thick layers of salt several kilometers beneath the seabed. About 5.3 million years ago, Atlantic water surged back through the Gibraltar Strait in a "Zanclean flood," possibly refilling the sea in just a few months to a few years.

cau_hoi: Which volcano in Iceland, known for multiple eruptions throughout history, was considered by medieval Europeans as the "gateway to hell"?
giai_thich: Hekla is one of the most active volcanoes in Iceland, having erupted more than 20 times since the Viking settlement in the 9th century. Medieval European monks and writers claimed that the volcano's mouth was the entrance to hell, where tormented souls were sent. The mountain's peak is often shrouded in clouds, which may be why the name Hekla means "the hooded cloak."

cau_hoi: What was the consequence of the Laki volcanic eruption in Iceland in 1783 – 1784?
B: Created the largest new island in Iceland
C: Toxic gases and famine caused about one-fifth of Iceland's population to die, with smoke spreading across Europe
giai_thich: Laki is a fissure about 27 km long, erupting massive amounts of lava and a lot of sulfur and fluorine gases. Poisoned grass led to the death of most livestock, resulting in a major famine. A haze spread across Europe in the summer of 1783, which may have contributed to a harsh winter and crop failures in many places. Benjamin Franklin, who was in Paris at the time, wrote about this unusual dry fog phenomenon.

cau_hoi: France and Italy have differing views on what regarding the summit of Mont Blanc?
A: Whether the exact border runs through the summit or the summit is entirely in France
B: The exact height of the mountain
C: The official name of the mountain
D: Who was the first to climb to the summit
giai_thich: The official map of France shows the border skewed towards Italy, making the summit entirely French, while the Italian map shows the border running through the summit. The dispute arises from differing interpretations of treaties and maps from the 19th century. The two countries still cooperate well in managing the area, but the question of "which country Mont Blanc belongs to" remains unanswered.

cau_hoi: In the towns of Baarle-Hertog (Belgium) and Baarle-Nassau (Netherlands), what is special about the border?
A: There is no border at all
B: It consists of dozens of territories nested within each other, with the border running through houses
D: The border is a high wall
giai_thich: Baarle-Hertog consists of 22 pieces of Belgian land located within Dutch territory, and within some of those pieces are 7 pieces of Dutch land. The border is marked by white crosses on the sidewalks, sometimes running through the middle of a café or living room. According to regulations, a house belongs to which country is determined by the position of the front door. This complexity stems from land agreements made in the medieval period.

cau_hoi: The town of Llívia is a detached territory of Spain located within France. Why was Llívia not ceded to France under the Treaty of the Pyrenees in 1659?
A: Because France did not want Llívia
B: Because Llívia is located on an island
C: Because the people of Llívia speak English
D: Because the treaty only ceded "villages", while Llívia is considered a "town"
giai_thich: The Treaty of the Pyrenees ceded 33 villages in the Cerdanya region to France. Since Llívia had the title of "town" from the time of Roman Emperor Charles V, the Spanish argued that it was not subject to cession. As a result, Llívia became a territory of Spain located a few kilometers from the border, connected to Spain by a "neutral" road. It is home to one of the oldest pharmacies in Europe.

cau_hoi: Büsingen am Hochrhein is a detached territory of Germany located within Switzerland. What is special about the people living here?
A: They do not pay any taxes
B: They use Swiss francs and are in the Swiss customs area despite being German territory
D: They speak French as the main language
giai_thich: Büsingen is surrounded by Switzerland and is only about 700 meters from the German border. Therefore, although legally part of Germany, daily life is closely tied to Switzerland: most residents use Swiss francs, and goods follow Swiss customs regulations. Interestingly, Büsingen has two postal codes (one for Germany and one for Switzerland), and the local football team competes in the Swiss league.

cau_hoi: The Balkan Peninsula is named after the Balkan mountain range (Stara Planina). In which country is this mountain range primarily located?
giai_thich: The Balkan mountain range is approximately 560 km long, running from the Serbian border eastward to the Black Sea, dividing Bulgaria into northern and southern halves. The name "Stara Planina" in Bulgarian means "Old Mountain". The highest peak is Botev, about 2,376 m. The mountain range has historically served as an important natural barrier, with famous passes such as the Shipka Pass.

cau_hoi: According to a popular explanation, why is the Picos de Europa mountain range in northern Spain called that?
A: A king named Europa named it
B: It was the first part of Europe that sailors returning from America saw
C: This is the highest mountain range in Europe
D: The mountains are shaped like a map of Europe
giai_thich: The Picos de Europa range is very close to the Bay of Biscay coast, so the limestone peaks rising about 2,600 m stand out on the horizon when ships return from the Atlantic. This was Spain's first national park (established in 1918), featuring deep gorges, caves, and home to brown bears and eagles. The region is also famous for Cabrales blue cheese aged in caves.

cau_hoi: The Landes forest in southwestern France, covering about one million hectares of maritime pine, is special for what reason?
A: The forest grows entirely on ice
B: This is the oldest primary forest in Europe
C: This is the largest man-made forest in Western Europe
D: This is the only tropical rainforest in Europe
giai_thich: In the 18th and 19th centuries, the Landes area was a swamp and poor sand dunes, where shepherds had to walk on stilts to move. Starting in 1857, under the law of Emperor Napoleon III, drainage canals were dug and pine trees were widely planted to stabilize the sand dunes and improve the soil. Today, the forest provides a lot of timber and pine resin, but as it is a monoculture forest, it is vulnerable to fires and storms.

cau_hoi: The Bonifacio Strait, about 11 km wide, separates which two large islands in the Mediterranean?
giai_thich: The Bonifacio Strait is famous for strong winds, currents, and many underwater rocks, making it very dangerous for ships. In 1855, the French warship Sémillante sank here, resulting in about 700 deaths. Today, the area is an international marine park jointly managed by France and Italy, and the passage of hazardous cargo ships is restricted. The town of Bonifacio is built on high white limestone cliffs right by the sea.

cau_hoi: The Otranto Strait, about 72 km wide, connects the Adriatic Sea with the Ionian Sea, located between Italy and which country?
giai_thich: The Otranto Strait lies between the "heel of the boot" of Italy (Puglia region) and the coast of Albania. This location is very important militarily as it can control access to the Adriatic Sea; during World War I, the Allies set up nets here to block submarines. On clear days, the mountains of Albania can be seen from Otranto across the sea.

cau_hoi: The Fehmarn Belt Tunnel currently under construction under the Baltic Sea will connect which two countries?
giai_thich: The tunnel, approximately 18 km long, will be the longest immersed tunnel (consisting of huge precast concrete sections placed on the seabed) in the world for both cars and trains. The tunnel connects Denmark's Lolland Island with Germany's Fehmarn Island, significantly reducing travel time between Copenhagen and Hamburg. The project is expected to be completed around the early 2030s.

cau_hoi: The Lærdal Tunnel, the longest road tunnel in the world (about 24.5 km), has what special feature to help drivers avoid drowsiness?
B: There are three large caverns illuminated with blue and yellow lights mimicking dawn
D: There are windows overlooking the sea
giai_thich: The Lærdal Tunnel in Norway was inaugurated in 2000, connecting Oslo with Bergen without having to cross the mountain passes often blocked by snow in winter. Driving for about 20 minutes in the tunnel can be tiring, so engineers designed three large caverns spaced evenly apart, illuminated with blue and yellow lights resembling the sky at dawn, helping drivers stay alert and making the journey feel shorter.

cau_hoi: Where is the highest peak in Portugal, a volcano approximately 2,351 m high, located?
C: In the Serra da Estrela mountains
giai_thich: Pico Mountain is a nearly perfect cone-shaped volcano rising from the bottom of the Atlantic Ocean. On the mainland of Portugal, the highest point is only about 1,993 m in the Serra da Estrela range. At the foot of Pico Mountain are vineyards planted between black basalt stone walls, which keep warmth and block sea winds, recognized by UNESCO as a World Heritage site.

cau_hoi: What mountain range is the highest peak of Ireland, Carrauntoohil (approximately 1,038 m), located in?
giai_thich: The MacGillycuddy's Reeks range is located in County Kerry, southwestern Ireland, formed from ancient red sandstone and shaped by glacial erosion, creating U-shaped valleys and glacial lakes. Carrauntoohil has a steel cross at its summit. The Mourne Mountains in Northern Ireland are believed to have inspired writer C.S. Lewis when he wrote about Narnia. The Grampian Mountains are in Scotland.

cau_hoi: What is the highest point of the Netherlands in Europe, Vaalserberg (approximately 322 m), known for?
A: The meeting point of three countries: the Netherlands, Belgium, and Germany
B: The meeting point of four countries: the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, and Luxembourg
C: The meeting point of two countries: the Netherlands and Belgium
D: The meeting point of five countries
giai_thich: At the summit of Vaalserberg, there is a tri-border marker where visitors can stand in all three countries at once. From 1816 to 1920, there was also a small neutral territory nearby called Moresnet due to a dispute over a zinc mine. The highest point of the entire Kingdom of the Netherlands is Scenery Mountain (approximately 887 m) on Saba Island in the Caribbean Sea.

cau_hoi: What mountain range does the highest peak in Switzerland, Dufourspitze (approximately 4,634 m), belong to?
giai_thich: Dufourspitze is the highest peak of the Monte Rosa massif located on the Swiss-Italian border and is the second highest peak in the Alps after Mont Blanc. The peak is named after General Guillaume-Henri Dufour, who directed the first accurate topographic map of Switzerland. The name "Monte Rosa" may derive from an ancient word meaning "glacier," not "pink."

cau_hoi: What title does Lake Hévíz in Hungary hold?
C: The deepest lake in the world
D: The largest natural thermal lake in the world suitable for swimming
giai_thich: Lake Hévíz covers about 4.4 hectares and is fed by a hot spring deep beneath the lake's surface, keeping the water warm, around 23–25°C in winter and 33–35°C in summer. The water is rich in minerals, and the lake's bottom mud is used for therapy. The lake is adorned with red lilies that bloom in summer, and people can swim even when it snows.

cau_hoi: Why is NASA interested in studying the Rio Tinto River in southern Spain, which has red and highly acidic water?
A: Because the river contains water from a meteorite
C: Because the river glows at night
D: Because microorganisms that can survive in this harsh environment may resemble life that once existed on Mars
giai_thich: The water of the Rio Tinto has a pH of about 2 (as acidic as lemon juice) and is red due to high levels of dissolved iron from the mines that have been exploited for about 5,000 years. Despite its harsh conditions, the river still hosts many microorganisms. Since Martian soil is also rich in iron and shows signs of having had acidic water, scientists use Rio Tinto as a testing ground for equipment searching for extraterrestrial life.

cau_hoi: What body of water was the Great Hungarian Plain (Alföld) once the bottom of about 10 million years ago?
giai_thich: The Pannonian Basin is surrounded by the Alps, Carpathians, and Dinaric Mountains. About 10 million years ago, it was a large inland sea, which gradually filled in with sediment from rivers, creating a flat, fertile plain. Today, the Hortobágy steppe on the plain, with grey cattle and twisted-horned sheep, is a national park and a UNESCO World Heritage site.

cau_hoi: Which major rivers originate in the Valdai Hills in northwestern Russia?
giai_thich: The Valdai Hills are not very high, only about 300–340 m, but they are an important watershed: the Volga River flows to the Caspian Sea, the Dnipro flows to the Black Sea, and the Western Dvina flows to the Baltic Sea. In the Middle Ages, Viking traders sailed from the Baltic Sea, dragging their boats across land in this region to reach rivers flowing south, creating the "route from the Varangians to the Greeks."

cau_hoi: Which sea is entirely within the territory of one country, connecting the Black Sea to the Aegean Sea through two straits?
giai_thich: The Marmara Sea covers about 11,350 km², entirely within Turkey, separating the European and Asian parts of the country. The sea's name comes from Marmara Island, which is famous for its marble quarries (the Greek word "marmaros" means marble). The sea lies on a major geological fault, making the surrounding area, including Istanbul, prone to earthquakes.

cau_hoi: Which country is Kotor Bay, often referred to as the "southernmost fjord in Europe," located in, and what type of terrain is it actually?
B: Montenegro – an ancient river valley flooded by seawater (ria)
D: Croatia – a fjord created by glaciers
giai_thich: Kotor Bay is surrounded by steep limestone mountains, resembling a fjord. However, geologists believe it is an ancient river valley that was submerged when sea levels rose, known as a "ria," rather than a true fjord carved by glaciers. The ancient town of Kotor, with its walls climbing the mountainside, is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

cau_hoi: What does the original Latin name of Cape Finisterre in Galicia (Spain), the endpoint for many pilgrims, mean?
giai_thich: The ancient Romans believed that this rocky promontory was the end of the land, with only the mysterious ocean beyond, hence it was called "Finis Terrae." Many pilgrims on the Camino de Santiago continue about 90 km from Santiago de Compostela to here to watch the sunset over the sea. In fact, Finisterre is not the westernmost point of Spain or Europe.
